      prune: true
      selfHeal: true

docs.title: Task 2.10: Validate locally
docs.text:
Files: none — verification.

  • Step 1: Render the kustomization
kustomize build apps/llama-cpp \
  --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec \
  > /tmp/llama-cpp-render.yaml

Expected: exit 0, file contains kind: Deployment, kind: Service, kind: Ingress, kind: Secret, kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy (×2), kind: Namespace.

  • Step 2: Spot-check critical fields
yq 'select(.kind == "Deployment") | .spec.template.spec.containers[0].image' /tmp/llama-cpp-render.yaml
yq 'select(.kind == "Deployment") | .spec.template.spec.initContainers[0].command' /tmp/llama-cpp-render.yaml
yq 'select(.kind == "Secret") | .metadata.name' /tmp/llama-cpp-render.yaml
yq 'select(.kind == "Ingress") | .spec.rules[0].host' /tmp/llama-cpp-render.yaml

Expected: - image is ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:<LLAMA_IMAGE_TAG> (with the tag substituted) - initContainer command contains the SHA256 placeholder filled in - Secret name is llama-cpp-env - Ingress host is llama.internal.neese-web.de

  • Step 3: Schema validation
scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh apps/llama-cpp

Expected: PASS.

  • Step 4: Pre-commit suite
git add apps/llama-cpp apps/argo-cd-apps/65-llama-cpp.yaml
pre-commit run --all-files

Expected: every hook PASS. The unencrypted-secret-detection hook in particular must NOT flag anything — if it does, an *.enc.yaml is not actually encrypted.

docs.title: Task 2.11: Register Application + Renovate + commit
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml - Modify: .github/renovate.json5

  • Step 1: Add the Application reference

Insert - 65-llama-cpp.yaml in the 65-block, alphabetically (e.g. above 65-postfix.yaml):

   - 65-headphones.yaml
+  - 65-llama-cpp.yaml
   - 65-nzbget.yaml

(Exact position may vary depending on which 65-* lines are currently uncommented; just keep the block roughly alphabetical.)

  • Step 2: Add Renovate manual-review for apps/llama-cpp/**

Same packageRule as Task 1.8 — the upstream ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp registry tags every commit, which would flood the PR queue without manual review.

 packageRules: [
   {
     matchFileNames: [
       'apps/mariadb/**',
       'apps/traefik/**',
       'apps/kubevip-ha/**',
       'apps/paperless-ai/**',
       'apps/pihole/**',
       'apps/monitoring-checkmk-server/**',
       'apps/argo-cd-apps-helm/**',
       'apps/nvidia-device-plugin/**',
+      'apps/llama-cpp/**',
     ],
     automerge: false,
   },
  • Step 3: Validate the parent kustomization
kustomize build apps/argo-cd-apps \
  --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec \
  > /dev/null

Expected: exit 0.

  • Step 4: Commit
git add apps/llama-cpp apps/argo-cd-apps/65-llama-cpp.yaml apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml .github/renovate.json5
git commit -m "feat(llama-cpp): add OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint on node04"

docs.title: Task 2.12: Push and observe
docs.text:
• Step 1: Push
git push origin main
  • Step 2: Wait for ArgoCD sync
until kubectl get application -n argocd 65-llama-cpp \
  -o jsonpath='SYNC={.status.sync.status} HEALTH={.status.health.status}{"\n"}' \
  | tee /dev/stderr | grep -q 'SYNC=Synced HEALTH=Healthy'; do
  sleep 15
done

If the app is OutOfSync for more than ~3 minutes, force refresh:

kubectl annotate -n argocd application 65-llama-cpp argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=hard --overwrite
  • Step 3: Verify pod state
kubectl get pods -n llama-cpp -l app=llama-cpp -o wide
kubectl describe pod -n llama-cpp -l app=llama-cpp | tail -40

Expected: pod is Running, both verify-model (Init) is Completed and the llama-cpp container is Ready. The pod must be on node04.

If the init container failed: kubectl logs -n llama-cpp -l app=llama-cpp -c verify-model will print which assertion fired (missing file / GGUF magic / SHA256 mismatch). Fix on node04, then either delete the pod or wait for the next backoff.

  • Step 4: Verify GPU consumption
kubectl get pod -n llama-cpp -l app=llama-cpp \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.containers[0].resources.requests.nvidia\.com/gpu}{"\n"}'
kubectl describe node node04 | grep -A4 "Allocated resources"

Expected: 1, and node04 shows 1/1 nvidia.com/gpu allocated.

docs.title: Task 2.13: HTTP smoke tests
docs.text:
• Step 1: Pull the API key
API_KEY=$(sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/llama-cpp/secrets.enc.yaml \
            | yq '.stringData.API_KEY')
test -n "$API_KEY" && echo "key length: ${#API_KEY}" || { echo "key empty!"; exit 1; }

Expected: key length: 64 (32 bytes hex-encoded).

  • Step 2: List models
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    https://llama.internal.neese-web.de/v1/models | jq

Expected: JSON with data: [ { id: "qwen2.5-coder-7b", ... } ].

  • Step 3: Chat completion
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    https://llama.internal.neese-web.de/v1/chat/completions \
    -d '{"model":"qwen2.5-coder-7b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with the single word: ok"}],"max_tokens":4}' \
    | jq '.choices[0].message.content'

Expected: a string containing ok (case-insensitive). First call may take 10–20 s if the model just loaded.

  • Step 4: Tool-calling smoke test (verifies --jinja)
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    https://llama.internal.neese-web.de/v1/chat/completions \
    -d '{
      "model": "qwen2.5-coder-7b",
      "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"What is the weather in Berlin?"}],
      "tools": [{
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "get_weather",
          "description": "Get the current weather for a city",
          "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["city"]
          }
        }
      }]
    }' | jq '.choices[0].message.tool_calls'

Expected: a non-null array containing one entry with function.name == "get_weather" and function.arguments decoding to {"city":"Berlin"} (the model's exact JSON formatting may vary).

  • Step 5: Auth-failure check
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
    https://llama.internal.neese-web.de/v1/models

Expected: 401 (no auth header). This proves the API key actually gates the endpoint and is not silently disabled.

docs.title: Self-Review
docs.text:
Run through this list before declaring the plan complete.

  • Spec coverage
  • Goal: OpenAI endpoint at llama.internal.neese-web.de with API key — Tasks 2.4 (key), 2.7 (Ingress), 2.13 (smoke).
  • Single fixed model Qwen2.5-Coder-7B Q4_K_M — Tasks 2.2 (download), 2.6 (args).
  • node-role/workload: zfs nodeSelector — Task 2.6.
  • runtimeClassName: nvidia + nvidia.com/gpu: 1 — Task 2.6 (workload), Task 1.4 (plugin).
  • Manual bootstrap of the model + SHA256 verification — Tasks 2.2, 2.6 (init container).
  • --parallel 1, --ctx-size 32768, q8_0 KV cache, --flash-attn — Task 2.6.
  • ksops + plain-encrypted Secret pattern — Task 2.4.
  • Plain networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress — Task 2.7.
  • Cilium default-deny + allow Traefik+DNS — Task 2.5.
  • Two ArgoCD Applications, waves 24 and 65 — Tasks 1.5, 2.9.

  • Renovate manual-review for both apps — Tasks 1.8, 2.11.

  • Placeholder scan

  • <CHART_VERSION> — resolved in Task 1.1, used in Task 1.4.
  • <LLAMA_IMAGE_TAG> — resolved in Task 2.1, used in Task 2.6.
  • <MODEL_SHA256> — resolved in Task 2.2, used in Task 2.6.

  • API key — generated in Task 2.1, encrypted in Task 2.4. No plaintext in repo.

  • Type / name consistency

  • Namespace llama-cpp — Tasks 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7.
  • Secret name llama-cpp-env and Secret key API_KEY — Tasks 2.4, 2.6.
  • Container port name http (8080) — Task 2.6 (probes), Task 2.5 (network policy targets 8080), Task 2.7 (Ingress targets 8080).
  • Service name llama-cpp — Task 2.6 (Service), Task 2.7 (Ingress backend).
  • Model file path /models/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf — Task 2.2 (host), Task 2.6 (init container, container, volume mount).
  • hostPath /zfs/llama-cpp/models — Task 2.2 (mkdir), Task 2.6 (volume).

  • NetworkPolicy endpointSelector for the workload (app: llama-cpp) matches the Deployment pod label — Tasks 2.5, 2.6.

  • Gates between phases

  • Phase 2 must not start until nvidia.com/gpu is 1 on node04 (end of Task 1.9).
  • Task 2.6 must not commit until Task 2.2 has produced <MODEL_SHA256>.

If anything in the above checklist points to a missing or contradictory step, fix it before handing the plan over.

docs.title: Open WebUI Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Deploy a multi-user Open WebUI in front of the existing llama-cpp deployment, authenticated via Authelia OIDC, with transparent Tavily web search for IDE clients.

Architecture: New ArgoCD application at sync wave 66 using the official open-webui Helm chart consumed via Kustomize helmCharts (Paperless pattern). SQLite on a Longhorn PVC, single replica, strategy: Recreate. Standard Ingress on chat.internal.neese-web.de with the hostname encrypted via SOPS. CiliumNetworkPolicy with default-deny plus targeted allows to llama-cpp and world:443.

Tech Stack: k3s 1.31.4, ArgoCD, Kustomize + Helm, Cilium, Longhorn, Traefik, Authelia OIDC, SOPS + age, ksops, Open WebUI Helm chart 14.6.0 (app 0.9.5).

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-20-open-webui-design.md

Note on TDD: This is infrastructure-as-code; there are no unit tests in the traditional sense. The "test" equivalent for each meaningful unit of work is kustomize build --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec plus scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh and pre-commit run. Verification steps are folded into the tasks accordingly.

docs.title: Task 1: Generate secrets and gather inputs
docs.text:
Files: none (interactive prep; values are consumed by Tasks 4 and 8)

This task is not committable. Gather everything up front so secrets never get pasted into chat or commit messages.

  • Step 1: Obtain Tavily API key

Sign in to https://app.tavily.com → API Keys → copy a key (starts with tvly-). Store privately for Task 4.

  • Step 2: Generate the Authelia OIDC client secret

Run: 

authelia crypto hash generate pbkdf2 --variant sha512 --iterations 310000 --random
Capture both lines from the output: - Password: <plaintext> — used in Task 4 (OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET) - Digest: $pbkdf2-sha512$310000$... — used in Task 8 (Authelia values)

  • Step 3: Generate WEBUI_SECRET_KEY

Run: 

openssl rand -hex 32
Store privately for Task 4. Rotating this value later logs every user out.

  • Step 4: Copy the existing llama-cpp API key

sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/llama-cpp/secrets.enc.yaml
Copy the API_KEY: value. Open WebUI calls llama-cpp with this same key. Store privately for Task 4.

docs.title: Task 2: Create namespace and default-deny network policy
docs.text:
Files: - Create: apps/open-webui/namespace.yaml - Create: apps/open-webui/k8s.np.open-webui-default-deny.yaml

  • Step 1: Create the namespace

Write apps/open-webui/namespace.yaml: 

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: open-webui
  labels:
    goldilocks.fairwinds.com/enabled: "true"

  • Step 2: Create the default-deny CiliumNetworkPolicy

Write apps/open-webui/k8s.np.open-webui-default-deny.yaml: 

---
# Default Deny Network Policy for namespace.
# Selecting all pods (empty endpointSelector) puts them under Cilium's
# default-deny semantics; the targeted policy in k8s.np.open-webui.yaml
# adds the specific allows we need.
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: open-webui-default-deny
  namespace: open-webui
spec:
  endpointSelector: {}
  ingress:
    - {}
  egress:
    - {}

docs.title: Task 3: Create the application-specific network policy
docs.text:
Files: - Create: apps/open-webui/k8s.np.open-webui.yaml

  • Step 1: Write the network policy
---
# Open WebUI application-specific network policy.
# Selecting the pod via endpointSelector puts it under Cilium default-deny;
# only explicitly allowed traffic passes.
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: open-webui
  namespace: open-webui
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: open-webui
  ingress:
    # Traefik forwards browser + IDE-API traffic.
    - fromEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:app.kubernetes.io/instance: traefik-kube-system
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: kube-system
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "8080"
              protocol: TCP
    # Same-namespace traffic (probes, helm post-install hooks).
    - fromEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: open-webui
  egress:
    # DNS via CoreDNS.
    - toEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.cilium.k8s.namespace.labels.kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: kube-system
            k8s:k8s-app: kube-dns
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "53"
              protocol: UDP
            - port: "53"
              protocol: TCP
    # llama-cpp backend (in-cluster).
    - toEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:app: llama-cpp
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: llama-cpp
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "8080"
              protocol: TCP
    # External HTTPS: Tavily API + Authelia OIDC discovery (the issuer URL
    # is the public hostname and must resolve via the external route, same
    # pattern Argo CD uses for its OIDC integration).
    - toEntities:
        - world
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "443"
              protocol: TCP

docs.title: Task 4: Create the SOPS-encrypted env secret
docs.text:
Files: - Create: apps/open-webui/secrets.enc.yaml (encrypted)

The Read tool is blocked on *.enc.yaml paths inside the repo. Use the /tmp workflow from CLAUDE.md to author the plaintext, then encrypt into the repo.

  • Step 1: Write the plaintext secret to /tmp
cat > /tmp/open-webui-secrets.enc.yaml <<'EOF'
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: open-webui-env
  namespace: open-webui
type: Opaque
stringData:
  # Auth / OIDC
  WEBUI_AUTH: "true"
  ENABLE_SIGNUP: "false"
  ENABLE_OAUTH_SIGNUP: "true"
  OAUTH_PROVIDER_NAME: "Authelia"
  OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: "openwebui"
  OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET: "<PASTE_AUTHELIA_CLIENT_SECRET_PLAIN_FROM_TASK_1_STEP_2>"
  OPENID_PROVIDER_URL: "https://auth.k8s.neese-web.de/.well-known/openid-configuration"
  OPENID_REDIRECT_URI: "https://chat.internal.neese-web.de/oauth/oidc/callback"
  OAUTH_SCOPES: "openid email profile groups"
  OAUTH_MERGE_ACCOUNTS_BY_EMAIL: "true"
  OAUTH_UPDATE_PICTURE_ON_LOGIN: "true"
  DEFAULT_USER_ROLE: "pending"

  # Session signing
  WEBUI_SECRET_KEY: "<PASTE_OPENSSL_RAND_HEX_32_FROM_TASK_1_STEP_3>"

  # llama-cpp backend
  ENABLE_OLLAMA_API: "false"
  OPENAI_API_BASE_URLS: "http://llama-cpp.llama-cpp.svc.cluster.local:8080/v1"
  OPENAI_API_KEYS: "<PASTE_LLAMA_CPP_API_KEY_FROM_TASK_1_STEP_4>"

  # Web search via Tavily
  ENABLE_RAG_WEB_SEARCH: "true"
  RAG_WEB_SEARCH_ENGINE: "tavily"
  TAVILY_API_KEY: "<PASTE_TAVILY_API_KEY_FROM_TASK_1_STEP_1>"
  RAG_WEB_SEARCH_RESULT_COUNT: "5"
  RAG_WEB_SEARCH_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS: "10"
  RAG_WEB_SEARCH_TRUST_ENV: "false"

  # Skip embedding/retrieval — Tavily snippets go directly into context
  BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL: "true"
EOF

Then open /tmp/open-webui-secrets.enc.yaml in an editor and replace the four <PASTE_*> placeholders with the actual values gathered in Task 1.

  • Step 2: Encrypt to the repo path
sops --config .sops.yaml -e /tmp/open-webui-secrets.enc.yaml > apps/open-webui/secrets.enc.yaml
  • Step 3: Verify round-trip

sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/open-webui/secrets.enc.yaml | diff - /tmp/open-webui-secrets.enc.yaml
Expected: no output (files identical).

  • Step 4: Wipe the plaintext temp file

: > /tmp/open-webui-secrets.enc.yaml
rm is not allowlisted; truncate-in-place is sufficient.

docs.title: Task 5: Create the encrypted Ingress
docs.text:
Files: - Create: apps/open-webui/ingress.enc.yaml (encrypted)

  • Step 1: Write the plaintext ingress to /tmp
cat > /tmp/open-webui-ingress.enc.yaml <<'EOF'
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: open-webui
  namespace: open-webui
  annotations:
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.entrypoints: web239,websecure239
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.tls: "true"
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.middlewares: traefik-redirect@kubernetescrd
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - chat.internal.neese-web.de
      secretName: wildcard-cloudflare-production-02
  rules:
    - host: chat.internal.neese-web.de
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: open-webui
                port:

EOF

The service port 80 matches the chart default (Service port 80 → containerPort 8080).

  • Step 2: Encrypt and verify

sops --config .sops.yaml -e /tmp/open-webui-ingress.enc.yaml > apps/open-webui/ingress.enc.yaml
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/open-webui/ingress.enc.yaml | diff - /tmp/open-webui-ingress.enc.yaml
: > /tmp/open-webui-ingress.enc.yaml
Expected: diff produces no output.

docs.title: Task 6: Create the ksops generator and Kustomize Helm chart
docs.text:
Files: - Create: apps/open-webui/kustomize-secret-generator.yaml - Create: apps/open-webui/kustomization.yaml

  • Step 1: Write the ksops generator
---
apiVersion: viaduct.ai/v1
kind: ksops
metadata:
  name: open-webui-secret-generator
  annotations:
    config.kubernetes.io/function: |
      exec:
        path: ksops
files:
  - secrets.enc.yaml
  - ingress.enc.yaml
  • Step 2: Write the kustomization
---
namespace: open-webui

resources:
  - namespace.yaml
  - k8s.np.open-webui-default-deny.yaml
  - k8s.np.open-webui.yaml

# injects the resources as if they were regular resources. The encrypted
# files are intentionally NOT in `resources:`.
generators:
  - kustomize-secret-generator.yaml

commonAnnotations:
  argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "66"

helmCharts:
  - name: open-webui
    repo: https://helm.openwebui.com/
    version: 14.6.0
    releaseName: open-webui
    namespace: open-webui
    includeCRDs: false
    valuesInline:
      ollama:
        enabled: false
      enableOpenaiApi: true
      ingress:
        enabled: false
      persistence:
        enabled: true
        size: 10Gi
        storageClass: longhorn
        accessModes:
          - ReadWriteOnce
      replicaCount: 1
      strategy:
        type: Recreate
      service:
        type: ClusterIP
        port: 80
      extraEnvFrom:

docs.text:
Files: - Modify: apps/authelia/values.enc.yaml (encrypted)

  • Step 1: Decrypt Authelia values to /tmp
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/authelia/values.enc.yaml > /tmp/authelia-values.enc.yaml
  • Step 2: Append the openwebui client block

Open /tmp/authelia-values.enc.yaml. Locate the existing list identity_providers.oidc.clients: (existing entries include argocd, grafana, semaphore). Append the following as a new list item, matching the surrounding indentation exactly (the existing entries are indented 16 spaces; the YAML below assumes that — adjust if the file uses different indentation):

            - client_id: openwebui
              client_name: Open WebUI
              client_secret: <PASTE_PBKDF2_DIGEST_FROM_TASK_1_STEP_2>
              claims_policy: default_claims_policy
              redirect_uris:
                - https://chat.internal.neese-web.de/oauth/oidc/callback
              scopes:
                - openid
                - profile
                - email
                - groups
              grant_types:
                - authorization_code
              response_types:
                - code
              authorization_policy: two_factor
              token_endpoint_auth_method: client_secret_post

Substitute the <PASTE_PBKDF2_DIGEST_*> placeholder with the Digest value (the $pbkdf2-sha512$... string), not the plaintext.

sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/authelia/values.enc.yaml | grep -A 2 "client_id: openwebui"
Expected: the new client block appears in the decrypted output.

kustomize build apps/authelia --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec > /dev/null
Expected: zero errors.

docs.title: Task 9: Write the WEBSEARCH.md runbook
docs.text:
Files: - Create: apps/open-webui/WEBSEARCH.md

  • Step 1: Write the runbook

Save the following as apps/open-webui/WEBSEARCH.md (content is in English per the repo convention):

# Open WebUI — Web Search Setup

This document explains the web-search wiring in this app and the post-deploy
steps required to expose it transparently to IDE clients (Continue.dev) via
the OpenAI-compatible API.

## Backend wiring

Open WebUI uses Tavily as the search backend. Configuration lives in the SOPS
secret `open-webui-env`:

- `ENABLE_RAG_WEB_SEARCH=true` — enables the web-search feature.
- `RAG_WEB_SEARCH_ENGINE=tavily` — selects Tavily as the provider.
- `TAVILY_API_KEY` — bearer key from https://app.tavily.com.
- `RAG_WEB_SEARCH_RESULT_COUNT=5` — snippets fetched per query.
- `RAG_WEB_SEARCH_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=10` — parallel fetches.

## Embedding bypass

`BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL=true` disables the embedding/retrieval layer
inside Open WebUI. Tavily snippets are inserted into the prompt context
verbatim, with no semantic chunking. This keeps the inference pipeline simple
and avoids running an embedding model on CPU (llama-cpp owns the GPU
exclusively and does not serve embeddings).

If you later want RAG over uploaded documents, the bypass must be turned off
and an embedding model deployed separately (e.g., a second llama.cpp instance
with `--embedding`, or a dedicated embedding service). That is out of scope
for the current setup.

## Virtual model `qwen2.5-coder-websearch`

Open WebUI does not enable web search per request by default. To make web
search transparent for IDE clients, create a virtual model with web search
toggled on:

1. Log in to https://chat.internal.neese-web.de as an admin user.
2. Workspace → Models → "Create a New Model".
3. Base Model: `qwen2.5-coder-7b` (exposed by the llama-cpp backend).
4. Model ID: `qwen2.5-coder-websearch`.
5. Capabilities → Web Search: **enabled**.
6. Save.

IDE clients target this virtual model. Every request goes through the Tavily
lookup automatically; the client does not need to know about web search.

> **Note:** this virtual model lives in the SQLite database on the Longhorn
> PVC. It is not represented in Git. If the PVC is destroyed, recreate the
> model by following these steps.

## IDE client setup (Continue.dev example)

Open WebUI → Settings → Account → API Keys → "Create new key".

In `~/.continue/config.json`:

```jsonc
"models": [{
  "title": "qwen-websearch",
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "qwen2.5-coder-websearch",
  "apiBase": "https://chat.internal.neese-web.de/api",
  "apiKey": "sk-<your personal Open WebUI key>"
}]
```

## Tavily Free tier

The Free plan covers 1000 calls/month. Track usage in the Tavily dashboard.
If you approach the limit, lower `RAG_WEB_SEARCH_RESULT_COUNT` and
`RAG_WEB_SEARCH_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`, or upgrade the plan.

docs.title: Downloader hostPath → Longhorn PVC Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Move the config volumes of headphones, lidarr, nzbget, nzbhydra2, radarr, sonarr, trailarr and unifi-controller from node-local hostPath directories onto dedicated Longhorn PVCs, without losing data and without breaking the hourly restic backup.

Architecture: Ten new ReadWriteOnce Longhorn PVCs, one per config tree. The cutover runs in two ArgoCD-visible commits with a manual copy step in between: first the PVCs are created and all eight Deployments are scaled to zero via Git, then one-off busybox Jobs copy each hostPath tree into its PVC with cp -a, then the Deployments are switched to the PVCs and scaled back up. The backup CronJob switches from six hostPath mounts to the same six PVCs, keeping the /backup/<app> mount paths so the encrypted RESTIC_SOURCE stays valid.

Tech Stack: k3s 1.36, ArgoCD, Kustomize, Longhorn (default StorageClass, 3 replicas, Retain), restic, busybox.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-downloader-hostpath-to-pvc-design.md

docs.title: Ground rules for this plan
docs.text:
• Never run kubectl edit/patch/apply against ArgoCD-managed objects. Everything reaches the cluster through Git. The only manual kubectl apply in this plan is the one-off migration Jobs, which no ArgoCD Application tracks.
  • git push and mutating kubectl are not available in the agent's shell. Every step that needs them is marked MANUAL (user) and the user runs it with the ! prefix.
  • Commits go straight to main. No Co-Authored-By or "Generated with" trailers.
  • ArgoCD Application names for the affected apps: 65-headphones, 64-downloader-lidarr, 65-nzbget, 65-nzbhydra2, 65-radarr, 65-sonarr, 34-trailarr, 65-unifi-controller.
  • unifi-controller lives in namespace media, not downloader. Its PVC, its migration Job and every kubectl -n … command for it use media. It has no backup today; Task 6b adds one modelled on Emby's, so it also joins the alerting and restore-test rotation.
  • Every Deployment keeps nodeSelector: node-role/workload: zfs, including nzbhydra2 and unifi-controller, which would otherwise be free of host storage after the migration. nzbhydra2's PVC is mounted by the shared, node-pinned downloader backup CronJob; unifi-controller is pinned by hostNetwork: true and the APs' inform IP. Do not remove either pin as a "cleanup".
  • Never paste decrypted secret values into chat or a commit message. Task 6b builds the unifi backup secret by piping SOPS output through sed, so no plaintext is ever printed or written into the repo.

docs.title: Task 2: Write the eight migration Jobs
docs.text:
Files: - Create: scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/README.md - Create: scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/headphones.yaml - Create: scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/lidarr.yaml - Create: scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/nzbget.yaml - Create: scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/nzbhydra2.yaml - Create: scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/radarr.yaml - Create: scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/sonarr.yaml - Create: scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/trailarr.yaml - Create: scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/unifi-controller.yaml

These files live outside apps/, so no ArgoCD Application picks them up. They are applied by hand once and deleted afterwards, and they are never committed — they only need to exist in the working tree long enough to run. Do not git add this directory in any commit.

The copy logic is identical in every Job — the same migrate() shell function, called once for single-volume apps and twice for nzbget and radarr. It is written inline in each file rather than shared, because each Job must be applyable on its own:

  1. skip the leg and return if ${dst}/.migration-complete exists, so a retry can still finish the legs that never ran. An exit here would kill the whole script: in a two-leg Job, a pod that died between leg 1 and leg 2 could then never be retried, because every attempt would stop at leg 1's guard
  2. abort if the target holds anything but lost+found and carries no marker — that is a half-finished copy from a dead attempt, and merging into it would produce a silently corrupt config
  3. cp -a "${src}/." "${dst}/" — preserves ownership, modes, timestamps
  4. replicate the source directory's own owner and mode onto the PVC root — a fresh Longhorn volume root is root:root 0755, but trailarr runs as UID 1000 and lidarr as UID 1001 and both need to create files directly in /config
  5. chmod 0755 "${dst}/lost+found" — ext4 creates it root:root 0700; the backup CronJob runs as UID 1000 and backup.sh runs under set -eEu -o pipefail, so restic's exit code 3 on an unreadable directory would fail every backup run and fire an ntfy alert
  6. touch "${dst}/.migration-complete" only after everything above succeeded

The container runs as root because the config trees are mixed-ownership, but it drops all capabilities except the three the copy actually needs: CHOWN for cp -a and the explicit chown, FOWNER for chmod on files owned by another UID, and DAC_OVERRIDE for reading mode-0700 directories such as radarr's and sonarr's config/xdg/.mono/. Dropping ALL without these — as the read-only backup CronJobs do — would make every Job fail.

  • Step 1: Write scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/README.md
# One-off hostPath → Longhorn PVC migration

These Jobs copy the downloader/trailarr config trees from the node-local
hostPath directories on node04 into their new Longhorn PVCs. They are **not**
managed by ArgoCD — apply them by hand, exactly once, while the Deployments are
scaled to 0.

```bash
# The apps must be at replicas: 0 first (see the plan, Task 3).
kubectl apply -f scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/

for ns in downloader media; do
  kubectl -n "$ns" get jobs -l app.kubernetes.io/component=migration
  kubectl -n "$ns" logs -l app.kubernetes.io/component=migration --tail=-1
done

# After the cutover is verified:
kubectl delete -f scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/
```

A Job whose legs all completed is marked and safe to re-apply — completed legs
are skipped. A Job that died mid-copy leaves unmarked data: re-applying will
abort with "holds unmarked data from a failed attempt". Recovery: delete the
failed Job, then clear the destination volume — the simplest way is to delete
the PVC and let ArgoCD recreate it (its Longhorn StorageClass uses `Retain`,
so the released PV must also be cleaned up in the Longhorn UI) — then
re-apply.

The source hostPath directories are mounted read-only and are never modified,
so nothing is ever lost by a failed attempt.
  • Step 2: Write scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/headphones.yaml
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: migrate-headphones-config
  namespace: downloader
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: migrate-headphones-config
    app.kubernetes.io/component: migration
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: migrate-headphones-config
        app.kubernetes.io/component: migration
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      nodeSelector:
        node-role/workload: zfs
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 0
        runAsGroup: 0
      containers:
        - name: copy
          image: busybox:1.37
          command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - |
              set -eu
              migrate() {
                src="$1"
                dst="$2"
                echo "==> ${src} -> ${dst}"
                # A finished leg carries a marker. Skip it and keep going so a
                # retry can still complete the legs that did not run yet.
                if [ -f "${dst}/.migration-complete" ]; then
                  echo "already migrated, skipping"
                  return 0
                fi
                # A fresh ext4 volume holds only lost+found. Anything else with
                # no marker is a half-finished copy from a dead attempt.
                if [ -n "$(ls -A "${dst}" | grep -v '^lost+found$' || true)" ]; then
                  echo "target ${dst} holds unmarked data from a failed attempt"
                  echo "clear the volume or recreate the PVC before retrying"
                  exit 1
                fi
                cp -a "${src}/." "${dst}/"
                # The Longhorn volume root is root:root 0755; take the source
                # directory's own owner and mode so non-root PUIDs can write.
                chown "$(stat -c '%u:%g' "${src}")" "${dst}"
                chmod "$(stat -c '%a' "${src}")" "${dst}"
                # ext4 creates lost+found as root:root 0700, which the restic
                # backup (UID 1000) cannot read.
                if [ -d "${dst}/lost+found" ]; then
                  chmod 0755 "${dst}/lost+found"
                fi
                touch "${dst}/.migration-complete"
                echo "==> done: $(du -sb "${dst}" | cut -f1) bytes"
              }
              migrate /src /dst
          volumeMounts:
            - name: src
              mountPath: /src
              readOnly: true
            - name: dst
              mountPath: /dst
          # Root is needed to chown/chmod to arbitrary UIDs and to read
          # config files with restrictive modes, but nothing beyond the
          # three capabilities that requires.
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            capabilities:
              drop:
                - ALL
              add:
                - CHOWN
                - DAC_OVERRIDE
                - FOWNER
            privileged: false
      volumes:
        - name: src
          hostPath:
            path: /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/headphones/config
            type: Directory
        - name: dst
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: longhorn-pvc-headphones-config

    app.kubernetes.io/component: migration
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: migrate-radarr-config
        app.kubernetes.io/component: migration
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      nodeSelector:
        node-role/workload: zfs
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 0
        runAsGroup: 0
      containers:
        - name: copy
          image: busybox:1.37
          command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - |
              set -eu
              migrate() {
                src="$1"
                dst="$2"
                echo "==> ${src} -> ${dst}"
                # A finished leg carries a marker. Skip it and keep going so a
                # retry can still complete the legs that did not run yet.
                if [ -f "${dst}/.migration-complete" ]; then
                  echo "already migrated, skipping"
                  return 0
                fi
                # A fresh ext4 volume holds only lost+found. Anything else with
                # no marker is a half-finished copy from a dead attempt.
                if [ -n "$(ls -A "${dst}" | grep -v '^lost+found$' || true)" ]; then
                  echo "target ${dst} holds unmarked data from a failed attempt"
                  echo "clear the volume or recreate the PVC before retrying"
                  exit 1
                fi
                cp -a "${src}/." "${dst}/"
                # The Longhorn volume root is root:root 0755; take the source
                # directory's own owner and mode so non-root PUIDs can write.
                chown "$(stat -c '%u:%g' "${src}")" "${dst}"
                chmod "$(stat -c '%a' "${src}")" "${dst}"
                # ext4 creates lost+found as root:root 0700, which the restic
                # backup (UID 1000) cannot read.
                if [ -d "${dst}/lost+found" ]; then
                  chmod 0755 "${dst}/lost+found"
                fi
                touch "${dst}/.migration-complete"
                echo "==> done: $(du -sb "${dst}" | cut -f1) bytes"
              }
              migrate /src/config /dst/config
              migrate /src/trailer /dst/trailer
          volumeMounts:
            - name: src-config
              mountPath: /src/config
              readOnly: true
            - name: src-trailer
              mountPath: /src/trailer
              readOnly: true
            - name: dst-config
              mountPath: /dst/config
            - name: dst-trailer
              mountPath: /dst/trailer
          # Root is needed to chown/chmod to arbitrary UIDs and to read
          # config files with restrictive modes, but nothing beyond the
          # three capabilities that requires.
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            capabilities:
              drop:
                - ALL
              add:
                - CHOWN
                - DAC_OVERRIDE
                - FOWNER
            privileged: false
      volumes:
        - name: src-config
          hostPath:
            path: /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/radarr/config
            type: Directory
        - name: src-trailer
          hostPath:
            path: /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/Trailer-Downloader-Config
            type: Directory
        - name: dst-config
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: longhorn-pvc-radarr-config
        - name: dst-trailer
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: longhorn-pvc-radarr-trailer-downloader

git push

Then wait for the sync (or force it): 

for a in 65-headphones 64-downloader-lidarr 65-nzbget 65-nzbhydra2 65-radarr 65-sonarr \
         34-trailarr 65-unifi-controller; do
  kubectl annotate -n argocd application "$a" argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=hard --overwrite

kubectl -n downloader get pvc | grep longhorn-pvc-
kubectl -n media get pvc | grep longhorn-pvc-unifi

kubectl -n media get deploy unifi-controller
kubectl -n downloader get pods
kubectl -n media get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=unifi-controller

docs.text:
Files: none (cluster operation)

  • Step 1: MANUAL (user) — apply the Jobs

kubectl apply -f scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/
Expected: eight job.batch/migrate-… created.

  • Step 2: MANUAL (user) — wait for completion

for ns in downloader media; do
  kubectl -n "$ns" wait --for=condition=complete --timeout=900s \
    job -l app.kubernetes.io/component=migration

Expected: eight condition met lines. radarr (1.2G) is the slowest.

  • Step 3: MANUAL (user) — read the logs

for ns in downloader media; do
  kubectl -n "$ns" logs -l app.kubernetes.io/component=migration --tail=-1
done
Expected: one ==> done: <bytes> bytes line per copied tree (ten in total). No target … is not empty lines.

  • Step 4: MANUAL (user) — compare the byte counts against Task 0

The done: byte counts must match the du -sb values recorded in Task 0 Step 2, within the size of lost+found (16 KiB per volume). A materially smaller number means the copy was incomplete — stop and investigate before continuing.

If a Job failed, delete the failed Job, fix the cause, wipe the target by deleting and letting ArgoCD recreate the PVC, and re-apply. The hostPath sources are untouched, so nothing is lost.

# All paths live on the ZFS host's local filesystem and are mounted
# read-only via hostPath. Pinned to the ZFS node via nodeSelector.
# Headphones and Epic Games are intentionally excluded — they are
# not mounted, so restic never sees them.

with

# Hourly backup of *arr-stack and downloader configs via restic.
# Every config tree is a ReadWriteOnce Longhorn PVC, mounted read-only.
# The nodeSelector below pins this Job to the same node as the workloads,
# which is what allows it to attach volumes those pods already hold.
# Headphones and Epic Games are intentionally excluded — they are
# not mounted, so restic never sees them.
  • Step 2: Replace the six config volumes

Replace

            - name: sonarr-config
              hostPath:
                path: /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/sonarr/config
                type: Directory
            - name: radarr-config
              hostPath:
                path: /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/radarr/config
                type: Directory
            - name: nzbget-config
              hostPath:
                path: /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/nzbget/config
                type: Directory
            - name: nzbhydra2-config
              hostPath:
                path: /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/nzbhydra2/config
                type: Directory
            - name: trailarr-config
              hostPath:
                path: /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/trailarr/config
                type: Directory
            - name: lidarr-config
              hostPath:
                path: /vol_raidz1/container-scheduler/downloader-lidarr
                type: Directory

with

            - name: sonarr-config
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: longhorn-pvc-sonarr-config
            - name: radarr-config
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: longhorn-pvc-radarr-config
            - name: nzbget-config
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: longhorn-pvc-nzbget-config
            - name: nzbhydra2-config
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: longhorn-pvc-nzbhydra2-config
            - name: trailarr-config
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: longhorn-pvc-trailarr-config
            - name: lidarr-config
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: longhorn-pvc-lidarr-config

The volumeMounts block is not changed: the mount paths stay /backup/sonarr, /backup/radarr, /backup/nzbget, /backup/nzbhydra2, /backup/trailarr, /backup/lidarr with readOnly: true, which is exactly what the encrypted RESTIC_SOURCE lists. The securityContext (runAsUser: 1000, runAsGroup: 1002, runAsNonRoot: true) also stays — cp -a preserved ownership and modes, so the group-bit access argument in the existing comment still holds.

  • Step 2b: Add lost+found and the migration marker to the exclude list

The downloader secret excludes asp, .mono, .bash_history and .__smb* but not lost+found. On a hostPath there was none; on an ext4-backed Longhorn volume there always is, and ext4 creates it root:root 0700. The migration Jobs chmod it to 0755, but that fix lives outside Git — if any of the six PVCs is ever recreated (restore, re-provision), the unreadable lost+found comes back and restic exits 3, failing the run and firing an ntfy alert. Excluding it removes the dependency entirely. The .migration-complete markers are excluded in the same pass so they never enter a snapshot.

Use Workflow B from CLAUDE.md — the EDITOR=sed form does not match this file:

T=/tmp/dl-backup.enc.yaml
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/downloader/nzbget/backup-secrets.enc.yaml > "$T"
sed -i 's|\(RESTIC_ADDITIONAL_BACKUP_PARAMETERS: .*\)$|\1 --exclude lost+found --exclude .migration-complete|' "$T"
sops --config .sops.yaml -e "$T" > apps/downloader/nzbget/backup-secrets.enc.yaml
: > "$T"

Verify without printing values — expect 1, 1, 12:

sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/downloader/nzbget/backup-secrets.enc.yaml \
  | grep -c -- "--exclude lost+found --exclude .migration-complete"
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/downloader/nzbget/backup-secrets.enc.yaml \
  | grep -c "^    RESTIC_SOURCE: /backup/sonarr /backup/radarr /backup/nzbget /backup/nzbhydra2 /backup/trailarr /backup/lidarr$"
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/downloader/nzbget/backup-secrets.enc.yaml \
  | grep -cE "^    (RESTIC|NTFY|PUSHGATEWAY)_"

Apply the same --exclude .migration-complete to apps/unifi-controller/backup-secrets.enc.yaml (it already excludes lost+found), so both secrets end up consistent.

Note: each sops -e produces a fresh MAC/IV, so the ciphertext changes even where the plaintext did not. That is expected.

  • Step 3: Verify the CronJob renders correctly

Run: 

kustomize build apps/downloader/nzbget --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec \
  | grep -E 'claimName: longhorn-pvc-|mountPath: /backup/'
Expected: six mountPath: /backup/… lines and, together with the Deployment's two, eight claimName: lines for the nzbget app.

  • Step 4: Confirm no downloader hostPath config mount is left anywhere

Run: 

grep -rn "docker/configs/downloader\|container-scheduler/downloader" apps/ \
  | grep -v "^apps/[^:]*k8s\.pvc\.yaml:"
Expected: no output. The k8s.pvc.yaml files are filtered out on purpose — each carries a comment naming the hostPath it replaced. Those are documentation, not mounts. Any hit outside them is a real leftover.

docs.title: Task 6b: Add a restic backup for unifi-controller
docs.text:
unifi-controller has never been backed up. Now that its config is a Longhorn PVC it can join the fleet using the same pattern as apps/emby/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml.

Files: - Create: apps/unifi-controller/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml - Create: apps/unifi-controller/backup-secrets.enc.yaml - Modify: apps/unifi-controller/kustomization.yaml - Modify: apps/unifi-controller/kustomize-secret-generator.yaml - Modify: apps/backup-script/k8s.backup-alerts.yaml - Modify: apps/backup-script/k8s.restore-test.yaml

  • Step 1: Write apps/unifi-controller/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml
---
# Hourly UniFi controller config backup via restic.
# Modelled on apps/emby/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml.
# Co-located with the unifi-controller pod via podAffinity because the
# Longhorn PVC is ReadWriteOnce.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: backup-unifi-controller
  namespace: media
spec:
  # The fleet is staggered per ten-minute slot; :25 is the free one
  # between grafana (:20) and emby (:30).
  schedule: "25 * * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 3600
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 2
      # 50 minutes
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 3000
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app.kubernetes.io/name: backup-unifi-controller
            app.kubernetes.io/component: backup
        spec:
          automountServiceAccountToken: false
          restartPolicy: Never
          # unifi-controller runs with PUID/PGID 1000, so every file under
          # /config is owned by 1000:1000 — no need to read as root.
          securityContext:
            runAsUser: 1000
            runAsGroup: 1000
            runAsNonRoot: true
          affinity:
            podAffinity:
              requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
                - labelSelector:
                    matchLabels:
                      app.kubernetes.io/name: unifi-controller
                  namespaces:
                    - media
                  topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          containers:
            - name: restic
              image: ghcr.io/madic-creates/container-restic:latest@sha256:5882ed8d36b4381ee2e6a7dad1a0c99f0341653a262209d655c69cee89770e62
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - /usr/local/bin/backup.sh
              env:
                - name: HOME
                  value: /home/restic
              envFrom:
                - secretRef:
                    name: backup-env-configuration-unifi
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backup-script
                  mountPath: /usr/local/bin/backup.sh
                  subPath: backup.sh
                - name: unifi-config
                  mountPath: /backup/unifi-controller
                  readOnly: true
                - name: home
                  mountPath: /home/restic
              securityContext:
                allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                capabilities:
                  drop:
                    - ALL
                privileged: false
          volumes:
            - name: unifi-config
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: longhorn-pvc-unifi-controller-config
            - name: backup-script
              configMap:
                name: crontab-backup-script
            - name: home
              # Node-disk cache, not RAM — same reasoning as the emby job:
              # restic's parent-snapshot working set outgrows a small memory
              # tmpfs and hits ENOSPC. Cache blobs are encrypted repo packs.
              emptyDir:
                sizeLimit: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: backup-unifi-controller
  namespace: media
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: backup-unifi-controller
  egress:
    - toEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.cilium.k8s.namespace.labels.kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: kube-system
            k8s:k8s-app: kube-dns
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "53"
              protocol: UDP
            - port: "53"
              protocol: TCP
    - toEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.cilium.k8s.namespace.labels.kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: monitoring
            k8s:app.kubernetes.io/name: prometheus-pushgateway
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "9091"
              protocol: TCP
    # Local restic REST-server (primary backup target)
    - toEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.cilium.k8s.namespace.labels.kubernetes.io/metadata.name: backup
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: backup
            k8s:app.kubernetes.io/name: rest-server
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "8000"
              protocol: TCP
    # ntfy notifications on failure
    - toEntities:
        - world
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "443"
              protocol: TCP
  • Step 2: Create the encrypted backup secret

The fleet shares one restic repository, password, ntfy and Pushgateway config, so the unifi secret is Emby's with three values changed. Build it by piping SOPS output through sed — no plaintext is ever printed to the terminal or written into the repo. Emby is also in namespace media, so the namespace needs no edit.

Run: 

sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/emby/backup-secrets.enc.yaml \
  | sed -e 's|^    name: .*|    name: backup-env-configuration-unifi|' \
        -e 's|^    RESTIC_SOURCE: .*|    RESTIC_SOURCE: /backup/unifi-controller|' \
        -e 's|^    RESTIC_HOSTNAME: .*|    RESTIC_HOSTNAME: unifi|' \
        -e 's|^    RESTIC_ADDITIONAL_BACKUP_PARAMETERS: .*|    RESTIC_ADDITIONAL_BACKUP_PARAMETERS: --tag unifi --exclude lost+found|' \
  > /tmp/unifi-backup.enc.yaml

sops --config .sops.yaml -e /tmp/unifi-backup.enc.yaml \
  > apps/unifi-controller/backup-secrets.enc.yaml

# rm is not allowlisted; truncate the plaintext temp file instead
: > /tmp/unifi-backup.enc.yaml

  • Step 3: Verify the secret without printing its values

Run: 

sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/unifi-controller/backup-secrets.enc.yaml \
  | grep -cE '^    (RESTIC|NTFY|PUSHGATEWAY)_'
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/unifi-controller/backup-secrets.enc.yaml \
  | grep -q 'name: backup-env-configuration-unifi' && echo "NAME OK"
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/unifi-controller/backup-secrets.enc.yaml \
  | grep -q 'RESTIC_SOURCE: /backup/unifi-controller' && echo "SOURCE OK"
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/unifi-controller/backup-secrets.enc.yaml \
  | grep -q 'RESTIC_HOSTNAME: unifi' && echo "HOSTNAME OK"
Expected: 12, then NAME OK, SOURCE OK, HOSTNAME OK.

  • Step 4: Wire the secret and the CronJob into the app

apps/unifi-controller/kustomize-secret-generator.yaml — add the new file: 

apiVersion: viaduct.ai/v1
kind: ksops
metadata:
  name: secret-generator
  annotations:
    config.kubernetes.io/function: |
      exec:
        path: ksops
files:
  - ingress.enc.yaml
  - backup-secrets.enc.yaml

apps/unifi-controller/kustomization.yaml — the full file after Task 1 Step 9 and this step: 

apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

namespace: media

resources:
  - k8s.pvc.yaml
  - k8s.deployment.yaml
  - k8s.service.yaml
  - k8s.np.unifi-controller.yaml
  - k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml

generators:
  - kustomize-secret-generator.yaml

  • Step 5: Teach the BackupNeverRun alert about unifi

In apps/backup-script/k8s.backup-alerts.yaml, replace

            or absent(backup_start_timestamp{instance="minecraft"})
            or absent(backup_start_timestamp{instance="restic-retentionpolicies"})

with

            or absent(backup_start_timestamp{instance="minecraft"})
            or absent(backup_start_timestamp{instance="unifi"})
            or absent(backup_start_timestamp{instance="restic-retentionpolicies"})

and in the same rule's description, replace

            description: "One or more of the expected backup instances has not pushed any metrics. Check CronJob status for: mariadb, emby, nextpvr, downloader, paperless, grafana, minecraft, restic-retentionpolicies."

with

            description: "One or more of the expected backup instances has not pushed any metrics. Check CronJob status for: mariadb, emby, nextpvr, downloader, paperless, grafana, minecraft, unifi, restic-retentionpolicies."
  • Step 6: Add unifi to the weekly restore test

In apps/backup-script/k8s.restore-test.yaml, replace

                  TAGS="mariadb emby nextpvr downloader paperless grafana minecraft"

with

                  TAGS="mariadb emby nextpvr downloader paperless grafana minecraft unifi"

and add a verifier branch immediately after the minecraft) branch, before the *) fallback:

                        unifi)
                          # system.properties is written by the controller for
                          # every site and lives directly under data/.
                          if [ ! -s "$TARGET/backup/unifi-controller/data/system.properties" ]; then
                            STATUS=1
                            FAIL_REASON="$TARGET/backup/unifi-controller/data/system.properties missing or empty"
                          fi ;;
  • Step 6b: Add unifi to the daily retention job

Without this, unifi-tagged snapshots are created hourly and never pruned — the per-app secrets set RESTIC_RETENTION_POLICIES_ENABLED: "false" and defer all forget/prune work to this one central CronJob.

In apps/backup-script/k8s.restic-retentionpolicies.yaml, replace

                  for TAG in mariadb emby nextpvr downloader paperless grafana minecraft; do

with

                  for TAG in mariadb emby nextpvr downloader paperless grafana minecraft unifi; do

and add the :25 slot to the schedule comment at the top of the file:

  # 03:05 daily. The other backup CronJobs are staggered around the hour
  # (mariadb :10, grafana :20, unifi :25, emby :30, nextpvr :40,
  # downloader :50, paperless :00); 03:05 lands in the gap before
  # mariadb's 03:10 slot.
  • Step 7: Verify the app builds with the CronJob and Secret

Run: 

kustomize build apps/unifi-controller --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec \
  | grep -E '^kind:|claimName:|name: backup-env-configuration-unifi'
Expected: a kind: PersistentVolumeClaim, kind: Deployment, kind: Service, kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy (twice — the app policy and the backup policy), kind: CronJob, kind: Secret, two claimName: longhorn-pvc-unifi-controller-config lines (Deployment and CronJob) and the generated secret name with its hash suffix.

  • Step 8: Schema-validate the touched apps

Run: 

scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh apps/unifi-controller
scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh apps/backup-script
Expected: both pass.

docs.title: Task 8: Commit B and cut over
docs.text:
Files: none beyond those already edited

  • Step 1: Run the pre-commit hooks

Run: 

pre-commit run --all-files
Expected: all hooks pass for the touched apps.

  • Step 2: Commit
git add apps/downloader/*/k8s.deployment.yaml \
        apps/trailarr/k8s.deployment.yaml \
        apps/unifi-controller/k8s.deployment.yaml \
        apps/unifi-controller/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml \
        apps/unifi-controller/backup-secrets.enc.yaml \
        apps/unifi-controller/kustomization.yaml \
        apps/unifi-controller/kustomize-secret-generator.yaml \
        apps/downloader/nzbget/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml \
        apps/downloader/nzbget/backup-secrets.enc.yaml \
        apps/backup-script/k8s.backup-alerts.yaml \
        apps/backup-script/k8s.restore-test.yaml \
        apps/backup-script/k8s.restic-retentionpolicies.yaml
git commit -m "feat(downloader,unifi): move config volumes to Longhorn PVCs and back up unifi"
  • Step 3: MANUAL (user) — push and sync
git push
for a in 65-headphones 64-downloader-lidarr 65-nzbget 65-nzbhydra2 65-radarr 65-sonarr \
         34-trailarr 65-unifi-controller; do
  kubectl annotate -n argocd application "$a" argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=hard --overwrite
done
  • Step 4: MANUAL (user) — verify sync and health

for a in 65-headphones 64-downloader-lidarr 65-nzbget 65-nzbhydra2 65-radarr 65-sonarr \
         34-trailarr 65-unifi-controller; do
  printf '%s ' "$a"
  kubectl get application -n argocd "$a" \
    -o jsonpath='SYNC={.status.sync.status} HEALTH={.status.health.status}{"\n"}'
done
kubectl -n downloader get pods -o wide
kubectl -n media get pods -o wide -l app.kubernetes.io/name=unifi-controller
Expected: every Application Synced / Healthy; all eight pods Running and 1/1 on node04.

  • Step 5: MANUAL (user) — verify each app sees its data

Open each web UI and confirm the library, indexers and history are intact: sonarr, radarr, lidarr, nzbget, nzbhydra2, trailarr, headphones.

For a quick check without the UI: 

kubectl -n downloader logs deploy/sonarr --tail=30
kubectl -n downloader logs deploy/radarr --tail=30
kubectl -n downloader logs deploy/trailarr --tail=30
kubectl -n media logs deploy/unifi-controller --tail=30
Expected: no database is locked, no permission denied, no fresh-install/first-run messages.

Give NZBGet's extension-script list one glance in its web UI (Settings → Extension Scripts). Unlike the other config volumes, that directory is actively scanned by the application, and the migration left a .migration-complete marker in it. The marker has no execute bit and no script header so NZBGet should ignore it — confirm rather than assume. For unifi, confirm the UI at https://192.168.1.45:8443 still shows the existing site and that the APs report as connected — a fresh setup wizard means the config did not come across.

  • Step 6: MANUAL (user) — verify the next backup run

The CronJob fires at :50. After it runs: 

kubectl -n downloader get jobs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=backup-downloader
kubectl -n downloader logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=backup-downloader --tail=50
Expected: Backup process completed, exit code 0, no permission denied on lost+found. If the run failed on lost+found, the migration Jobs' chmod did not apply to that volume — fix it with a one-off debug pod that mounts the PVC and runs chmod 0755 /mnt/lost+found.

To trigger it immediately instead of waiting: 

kubectl -n downloader create job --from=cronjob/backup-downloader backup-downloader-manual

  • Step 7: MANUAL (user) — verify the new unifi backup

The new CronJob fires at :25. Trigger it immediately instead: 

kubectl -n media create job --from=cronjob/backup-unifi-controller backup-unifi-manual
kubectl -n media logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=backup-unifi-controller --tail=50
Expected: Backup process completed and exit code 0. Then confirm the snapshot and its tag exist — run this from any pod that already has the restic env, e.g. the retention CronJob's image, or check the Grafana backup dashboard for an instance="unifi" series appearing after the run.

A first run has no parent snapshot, so it uploads all ~372 MB and takes longer than later incremental runs.

docs.title: Task 9: Clean up
docs.text:
Files: - Delete: scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/ (after the migration is verified)

  • Step 1: MANUAL (user) — delete the migration Jobs from the cluster
kubectl delete -f scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/
  • Step 2: MANUAL (user) — delete the migration manifests from the working tree

They were never committed, so this is a plain filesystem delete with nothing to push:

rm -r scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/
git status --short   # the directory should simply disappear from the untracked list
  • Step 3: MANUAL (user, optional) — remove the migration markers

Each migrated volume keeps a zero-byte .migration-complete file in its root. It is harmless, but removing it is tidy and makes a stray re-apply of the Jobs abort loudly instead of silently skipping:

kubectl -n downloader exec deploy/sonarr     -- rm -f /config/.migration-complete
kubectl -n downloader exec deploy/radarr     -- rm -f /config/.migration-complete
kubectl -n downloader exec deploy/lidarr     -- rm -f /config/.migration-complete
kubectl -n downloader exec deploy/nzbhydra2  -- rm -f /config/.migration-complete
kubectl -n downloader exec deploy/headphones -- rm -f /config/.migration-complete
kubectl -n downloader exec deploy/trailarr   -- rm -f /config/.migration-complete
kubectl -n downloader exec deploy/nzbget     -- rm -f /config/.migration-complete /app/nzbget/scripts/.migration-complete
kubectl -n media      exec deploy/unifi-controller -- rm -f /config/.migration-complete

nzbget's scripts volume is mounted read-only in the container, so its marker cannot be removed this way — leave it, or clear it with a short-lived debug pod that mounts the PVC read-write. radarr's trailer-downloader marker is invisible to the container (the volume is mounted with subPath: settings.ini) and needs the same debug-pod treatment if you care.

Do this only after the migration is confirmed good — while the markers are in place, re-applying a Job is a safe no-op.

  • Step 4: Leave the old hostPath data in place

The source directories on node04 are the fallback. Delete them only after several days of confirmed-good operation and at least one verified restic restore test:

ssh mne-adm@192.168.1.24 'sudo rm -rf \
  /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/{headphones,nzbget,nzbhydra2,radarr,sonarr,trailarr} \
  /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/Trailer-Downloader-Config \
  /vol_raidz1/container-scheduler/downloader-lidarr \
  /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/unify-controller'

Do not run this as part of the migration. /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/lidarr/config (899M, stale — the running lidarr used container-scheduler/downloader-lidarr) and the tdarr/tdarr2 directories are out of scope and must not be deleted here.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Before Task 5 is pushed: nothing is lost. git revert the Commit A hash, push, and the Deployments come back on their hostPath volumes with the original data.

After Task 8 is pushed: git revert the Commit B hash and push. The Deployments return to the hostPath volumes; that data is stale by however long the apps ran on the PVCs. The PVCs are untouched by the revert, and the longhorn StorageClass uses Retain, so the migrated data survives even a PVC delete and can be re-attached via a longhorn-static PV.

docs.title: td-sync Server Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Run the td sync server (github.com/marcus/td) in the k3s home cluster, reachable only from the internal network, with automated version updates via Renovate and file-level backups via restic.

Architecture: Two repositories. madic/docker-td on forge.geekbundle.org builds the container image (upstream publishes none) via Forgejo Actions; its Dockerfile clones the upstream at a pinned ARG TD_VERSION that Renovate maintains. k3s-git-ops/apps/td-sync/ deploys that image via ArgoCD: one Longhorn PVC, single replica, Traefik ingress on the internal entrypoints, Cilium default-deny, and an hourly restic CronJob that snapshots the SQLite databases consistently before shipping them.

Tech Stack: Go (upstream build only), SQLite + Litestream, Docker, Forgejo Actions, Renovate, Kubernetes 1.36 (k3s), Kustomize + ksops + SOPS/age, ArgoCD, Cilium, Longhorn, restic, Traefik.

Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-td-sync-server-design.md td issue: td-02c66e

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Two working directories. Build repo: /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/docker-td (remote ssh://git@forge.geekbundle.org/madic/docker-td.git, branch main). Cluster repo: /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops (branch main).
  • Never bypass ArgoCD. No kubectl edit/patch/apply on managed objects. Change YAML → commit → push → sync. Read-only kubectl get/logs/describe/exec and kubectl create job --from=cronjob/... are fine.
  • In k3s-git-ops, push approved changes straight to main, no PR. Rebase before pushing — the remote runs ahead.
  • No Co-Authored-By or "Generated with" trailers in commits.
  • End every git commit message with: Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JTJMgDKXYPLzeS5Z7wFtgS
  • Do not commit anything under docs/superpowers/ — specs and plans stay local.
  • Never paste decrypted secret values into chat, commit messages, or plan files.
  • The Read tool is blocked on *.enc.yaml inside the repo. Use the two SOPS workflows from CLAUDE.md: EDITOR='sed -i ...' sops --config .sops.yaml <file> for small edits, or decrypt to /tmp/*.enc.yaml → edit → re-encrypt for structural ones. rm is not allowlisted; blank temp files with : > /tmp/file.

docs.title: Task 1: Build repo — Dockerfile
docs.text:
Produces the image definition. The ARG TD_VERSION line is what Renovate edits later, so its exact shape matters.

Files: - Create: /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/docker-td/Dockerfile - Modify: /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/docker-td/README.md

Interfaces: - Consumes: nothing. - Produces: Dockerfile containing exactly one line matching ^ARG TD_VERSION="(.*)"$. Task 2's workflow extracts the version with that pattern. Runtime image contains /usr/local/bin/td-sync, /usr/local/bin/litestream, /entrypoint.sh, /etc/litestream.yml, and the sqlite3 binary. Listens on 8080, data in /data, Litestream file replica in /backups.

  • Step 1: Verify the base image tags exist before writing anything

The upstream Dockerfile pins golang:1.27-alpine and litestream/litestream:0.3.13. If either tag is missing, the build fails with an unhelpful error. Check first:

for ref in "library/golang:1.27-alpine" "litestream/litestream:0.3.13" "library/alpine:3.21"; do
  repo="${ref%:*}"; tag="${ref##*:}"
  tok=$(curl -s "https://auth.docker.io/token?service=registry.docker.io&scope=repository:${repo}:pull" \
        | sed -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $tok" \
         -H 'Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json' \
         "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/${repo}/manifests/${tag}")
  echo "$ref -> HTTP $code"
done

Expected: HTTP 200 for all three.

If golang:1.27-alpine returns 404, pick the highest available golang:1.2x-alpine that satisfies the upstream go.mod (check with curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marcus/td/v0.65.0/go.mod | head -5) and use that instead. Note the substitution in the commit message. Do not fall back to golang:alpine — an unpinned tag defeats Renovate's Dockerfile manager.

  • Step 2: Write the Dockerfile
# Build the td sync server from upstream sources.
#
# Upstream (github.com/marcus/td) publishes release binaries but no container
# image, so we build our own. The version below is the single source of truth:
# Renovate bumps it, and .forgejo/workflows/build.yaml derives the image tag
# from it.
#
# This differs from upstream's deploy/Dockerfile in two ways:
#   1. We clone the sources here instead of building from the build context,
#      which keeps TD_VERSION in one Renovate-maintainable line.
#   2. sqlite is added to the runtime image. The backup CronJob in k3s-git-ops
#      reuses this image as an initContainer to produce consistent `.backup`
#      copies of the WAL databases before restic ships them.

# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=marcus/td
ARG TD_VERSION="v0.65.0"

# --- Build stage ---
FROM golang:1.27-alpine AS builder

# A global ARG is not visible inside a stage unless re-declared without a value.
ARG TD_VERSION

RUN apk add --no-cache git

WORKDIR /src
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "${TD_VERSION}" https://github.com/marcus/td.git .
RUN go mod download
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/td-sync ./cmd/td-sync

# --- Litestream stage ---
FROM litestream/litestream:0.3.13 AS litestream

# --- Runtime stage ---
FROM alpine:3.21

RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates tzdata wget sqlite

COPY --from=litestream /usr/local/bin/litestream /usr/local/bin/litestream
COPY --from=builder /out/td-sync /usr/local/bin/td-sync
COPY --from=builder /src/deploy/litestream.yml /etc/litestream.yml
COPY --from=builder /src/deploy/entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod +x /entrypoint.sh

VOLUME /data
EXPOSE 8080

ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]
  • Step 3: Verify the version line matches what the workflow and Renovate expect

Two consumers depend on this line's exact shape. Check both.

The workflow's extraction:

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/docker-td
sed -n 's/^ARG TD_VERSION="\(.*\)"/\1/p' Dockerfile | head -1

Expected output: v0.65.0 — exactly one line, no quotes, nothing else.

Renovate's customManagers:dockerfileVersions preset regex:

python3 - <<'PY'
import re, pathlib
rx = re.compile(
    r"# renovate: datasource=(?P<datasource>[a-zA-Z0-9-._]+?) depName=(?P<depName>[^\s]+?)"
    r"(?: (?:lookupName|packageName)=(?P<packageName>[^\s]+?))?"
    r"(?: versioning=(?P<versioning>[^\s]+?))?"
    r"(?: extractVersion=(?P<extractVersion>[^\s]+?))?"
    r"(?: registryUrl=(?P<registryUrl>[^\s]+?))?"
    r"\s(?:ENV|ARG)\s+[A-Za-z0-9_]+?_VERSION[ =][\"']?(?P<currentValue>.+?)[\"']?\s"
)
m = rx.search(pathlib.Path("Dockerfile").read_text())
print(m.groupdict() if m else "NO MATCH - Renovate will not track TD_VERSION")
PY

Expected: {'datasource': 'github-releases', 'depName': 'marcus/td', ..., 'currentValue': 'v0.65.0'}.

If this prints NO MATCH, the comment and ARG line are malformed — fix them before continuing. A silent non-match here means the whole update automation is dead on arrival, and nothing later in this plan will surface it.

  • Step 4: Write the README
# docker-td

Container image for the [td](https://github.com/marcus/td) sync server.

Upstream publishes release binaries but no container image, so this repo builds
one from `deploy/Dockerfile`'s recipe, with sqlite added to the runtime image
for consistent SQLite backups.

Image: `forge.geekbundle.org/madic/td-sync`

## Updating

`ARG TD_VERSION` in the `Dockerfile` is the single source of truth. The update
chain runs by itself:

1. Renovate (`.forgejo/workflows/renovate.yaml`) bumps `ARG TD_VERSION`
2. Branch automerge lands it on `main`
3. `.forgejo/workflows/build.yaml` builds and pushes `td-sync:<version>`
4. Renovate in `madic-creates/k3s-git-ops` bumps tag and digest in
   `apps/td-sync/k8s.td-sync.yaml`

Minor bumps of `marcus/td` are **not** automerged — td is on `0.x`, where a
minor bump may break. They land as a pull request for review.

Deployment lives in `madic-creates/k3s-git-ops` under `apps/td-sync/`.

git add Dockerfile README.md
git commit -m "feat: add Dockerfile building td-sync from pinned upstream tag

Upstream publishes no container image. The Dockerfile clones marcus/td at
ARG TD_VERSION so Renovate can maintain the version in one line, and adds
sqlite to the runtime image for consistent SQLite backups.

docs.title: Task 2: Build repo — Forgejo Actions build workflow
docs.text:
Files: - Create: /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/docker-td/.forgejo/workflows/build.yaml

Interfaces: - Consumes: Dockerfile from Task 1, specifically the ^ARG TD_VERSION="(.*)"$ line. - Produces: forge.geekbundle.org/madic/td-sync:<version> and :latest in the Forgejo container registry. Task 4 needs the <version> and the manifest digest.

Why no docker/* actions: uses: references resolve against the Forgejo instance's DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL, which defaults to code.forgejo.org where the docker/* actions do not exist. Plain docker CLI steps work regardless. actions/checkout is the one exception — it is mirrored on both code.forgejo.org and GitHub.

  • Step 1: Write the workflow
---
name: Build td-sync

# Path-filtered so Renovate's base-image bumps and TD_VERSION bumps both
# trigger a build, but README-only commits do not.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "Dockerfile"
      - ".forgejo/workflows/build.yaml"
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  REGISTRY: forge.geekbundle.org
  IMAGE_NAME: madic/td-sync

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The Dockerfile is the single source of truth for the version, so the
      # image tag is derived from it rather than duplicated here.
      - name: Resolve td version from Dockerfile
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version=$(sed -n 's/^ARG TD_VERSION="\(.*\)"/\1/p' Dockerfile | head -1)
          if [ -z "$version" ]; then
            echo "Could not read ARG TD_VERSION from Dockerfile" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Building td-sync $version"

      - name: Log in to the Forgejo container registry
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            | docker login "$REGISTRY" -u "${{ github.actor }}" --password-stdin

      - name: Build and push
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          image="$REGISTRY/$IMAGE_NAME"
          version="${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}"
          docker build -t "$image:$version" -t "$image:latest" .
          docker push "$image:$version"
          docker push "$image:latest"

      # Printed so the digest can be copied into k3s-git-ops without a
      # separate registry query.
      - name: Report the pushed digest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' \
            "$REGISTRY/$IMAGE_NAME:${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}"

docs.title: Task 3: Build repo — Renovate
docs.text:
Files: - Create: /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/docker-td/renovate.json5 - Create: /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/docker-td/.forgejo/workflows/renovate.yaml

Interfaces: - Consumes: the # renovate: / ARG TD_VERSION pair from Task 1. - Produces: commits on main that bump ARG TD_VERSION or the base image tags, which trigger Task 2's workflow.

  • Step 1: Create the two Forgejo secrets

In the repo settings of madic/docker-td → Actions → Secrets:

Secret Value RENOVATE_TOKEN Forgejo PAT. Scopes: repo (read+write), user (read), issue (read+write), organization (read), read:packages GITHUB_COM_TOKEN GitHub PAT, public-repo read-only, no scopes needed beyond default

GITHUB_COM_TOKEN is not optional. The github-releases datasource queries github.com even though the platform is Forgejo, and unauthenticated requests hit the rate limit quickly — Renovate then silently reports no updates rather than failing.

  • Step 2: Write the Renovate config
{
  $schema: 'https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json',
  onboarding: false,
  requireConfig: 'ignored',
  extends: [
    'config:recommended',
    // Matches `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` followed by
    // `ARG <NAME>_VERSION="..."`. This is what tracks TD_VERSION.
    'customManagers:dockerfileVersions',
  ],
  platform: 'forgejo',
  endpoint: 'https://forge.geekbundle.org/api/v1',
  repositories: [
    'madic/docker-td',
  ],
  gitAuthor: 'Renovate Bot <bot@renovateapp.com>',
  prConcurrentLimit: 0,
  prHourlyLimit: 0,
  automerge: true,
  automergeType: 'branch',
  // Forgejo supports platform-native automerge only from v10; Renovate's own
  // branch automerge works regardless.
  platformAutomerge: false,
  ignoreTests: true,
  major: {
    automerge: false,
  },
  minor: {
    automerge: true,
  },
  patch: {
    automerge: true,
  },
  packageRules: [
    {
      // td is on 0.x, where a minor bump is allowed to break things. Do not
      // rely on Renovate classifying 0.x minors as major - say it explicitly.
      matchDepNames: [
        'marcus/td',
      ],
      matchUpdateTypes: [
        'minor',
      ],
      automerge: false,
    },
  ],
  minimumReleaseAge: '5 days',
  minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: 'timestamp-optional',
  internalChecksFilter: 'strict',
}
  • Step 3: Write the Renovate workflow
---
name: Renovate

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 4 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: "Dry run (no commits)"
        required: true
        default: "false"
        type: choice
        options:
          - "false"
          - "true"

concurrency:
  group: renovate
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  renovate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run Renovate
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "${{ inputs.dryRun }}" = "true" ]; then
            export RENOVATE_DRY_RUN=full
          fi
          npx --yes renovate
        env:
          RENOVATE_CONFIG_FILE: renovate.json5
          RENOVATE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RENOVATE_TOKEN }}
          # The github-releases datasource queries github.com regardless of
          # platform; without a token it rate-limits and reports no updates.
          GITHUB_COM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_COM_TOKEN }}
          LOG_LEVEL: info

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/docker-td
git add renovate.json5 .forgejo/workflows/renovate.yaml
git commit -m "ci: track td and base image versions with Renovate

Read the job log and confirm all four dependencies are found:

docs.text:
The largest task, and deliberately so: namespace, PVC, deployment, service, ingress and network policies have no independent value. A reviewer accepts or rejects "td-sync answers /healthz behind the internal ingress" as one unit.

  • Step 1: Write the PVC

apps/td-sync/k8s.pvc.yaml:

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: longhorn-pvc-td-sync
  namespace: td-sync

    app.kubernetes.io/name: td-sync
