  • Step 2: Write the workload manifests

apps/td-sync/k8s.td-sync.yaml:

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: td-sync
  labels:
    goldilocks.fairwinds.com/enabled: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: td-sync
  namespace: td-sync
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: td-sync
  namespace: td-sync
spec:
  revisionHistoryLimit: 3
  replicas: 1
  # SQLite tolerates exactly one writer and the Longhorn PVC is ReadWriteOnce.
  # A RollingUpdate would briefly run two pods; Recreate keeps it at one.
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: td-sync
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: td-sync
    spec:
      serviceAccount: td-sync
      # The upstream image sets no USER and would run as root. fsGroup makes
      # the Longhorn volume writable for UID 1000 instead.
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 1000
        runAsGroup: 1000
        fsGroup: 1000
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
        - name: td-sync
          # https://github.com/marcus/td
          # Built by forge.geekbundle.org/madic/docker-td
          # Tag AND digest: a digest-only reference gives Renovate no
          # currentValue and the image stops being tracked.
          image: forge.geekbundle.org/madic/td-sync:v0.65.0@sha256:REPLACE_WITH_DIGEST_FROM_TASK_2
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: http
          env:
            - name: SYNC_LISTEN_ADDR
              value: ":8080"
            # Must match the ingress host: it is embedded in the login
            # verification links.
            - name: SYNC_BASE_URL
              value: "https://td.internal.neese-web.de"
            - name: SYNC_SERVER_DB_PATH
              value: "/data/server.db"
            - name: SYNC_PROJECT_DATA_DIR
              value: "/data/projects"
            # Flipped to "false" in Task 5 once the first account exists.
            - name: SYNC_ALLOW_SIGNUP
              value: "true"
            # td supports cloudflare, log and memory only - no SMTP, so the
            # in-cluster Postfix relay cannot be used. The verification link
            # is read from this pod's log.
            - name: SYNC_EMAIL_PROVIDER
              value: "log"
            - name: SYNC_LOG_FORMAT
              value: "json"
            - name: SYNC_LOG_LEVEL
              value: "info"
            - name: SYNC_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT
              value: "60s"
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 30
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 64Mi
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            capabilities:
              drop:
                - ALL
            privileged: false
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
              subPath: data
            # The entrypoint always starts Litestream. Giving /backups a real
            # mount means the file replica of server.db survives restarts and
            # is picked up by the restic job.
            - name: data
              mountPath: /backups
              subPath: backups
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: longhorn-pvc-td-sync
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: td-sync
  namespace: td-sync
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: td-sync
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    - port: 8080
      name: http
      targetPort: http
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: td-sync

Replace REPLACE_WITH_DIGEST_FROM_TASK_2 with the digest captured in Task 2 Step 5.

---
# td-sync Network Policy
#
# td-sync talks to nobody: the `log` email provider sends no mail, Litestream
# replicates to the local filesystem only, and there are no outbound calls.
# DNS egress is all it needs.
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: td-sync
  namespace: td-sync
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: td-sync
  ingress:
  # Allow ingress from Traefik. The blackbox probe added in Task 8 also
  # arrives through Traefik, so it needs no separate rule.
  - fromEndpoints:
    - matchLabels:
        k8s:app.kubernetes.io/instance: traefik-kube-system
        k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: kube-system
    toPorts:
    - ports:
      - port: "8080"
        protocol: TCP
  egress:
  # Allow DNS resolution via CoreDNS
  - toEndpoints:
    - matchLabels:
        k8s:io.cilium.k8s.namespace.labels.kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
        k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: kube-system
        k8s:k8s-app: kube-dns
    toPorts:
    - ports:
      - port: "53"
        protocol: UDP
      - port: "53"
        protocol: TCP
  • Step 4: Write the encrypted ingress

The hostname is encrypted by .sops.yaml's encrypted_regex (it matches hosts? and host). Write plaintext first, then encrypt in place.

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
mkdir -p apps/td-sync
cat > apps/td-sync/ingress.enc.yaml <<'EOF'
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: td-sync
  namespace: td-sync
  annotations:
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.entrypoints: web239,websecure239
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.tls: "true"
    # Deliberately no authelia-forwardauth middleware: the td CLI
    # authenticates with a bearer token against /v1/... and cannot follow an
    # SSO redirect. td brings its own auth (device flow + API keys).
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.middlewares: traefik-redirect@kubernetescrd
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - td.internal.neese-web.de
      secretName: wildcard-cloudflare-production-02
  rules:
    - host: td.internal.neese-web.de
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: td-sync
                port:
                  number: 8080
EOF
sops --config .sops.yaml -e -i apps/td-sync/ingress.enc.yaml

Verify it round-trips and that the hostname is actually encrypted:

sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/td-sync/ingress.enc.yaml | grep -c 'td.internal.neese-web.de'
grep -c 'td.internal.neese-web.de' apps/td-sync/ingress.enc.yaml

Expected: 2 from the first command (tls host + rule host), 0 from the second. A non-zero second result means the hostname is sitting in the repo in plaintext — fix before committing.

  • Step 5: Write the kustomization files

apps/td-sync/kustomize-secret-generator.yaml:

---
apiVersion: viaduct.ai/v1
kind: ksops
metadata:
  name: secret-generator
  annotations:
    config.kubernetes.io/function: |
      exec:
        path: ksops
files:
  - ingress.enc.yaml

apps/td-sync/kustomization.yaml:

---
commonAnnotations:
  argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "62"

resources:
  - k8s.td-sync.yaml
  - k8s.pvc.yaml
  - k8s.np.td-sync-default-deny.yaml
  - k8s.np.td-sync.yaml

generators:
  - kustomize-secret-generator.yaml

Task 7 adds the backup CronJob and its secret to both files.

  • Step 6: Write the ArgoCD Application

apps/argo-cd-apps/62-td-sync.yaml:

---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: 62-td-sync
  namespace: argocd
  finalizers:
    - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "62"
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: "example.com"
    path: apps/td-sync
    targetRevision: HEAD
  destination:
    server: "https://kubernetes.default.svc"
    namespace: default
  syncPolicy:
    syncOptions:
      - ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true

repoURL: "example.com" is not a mistake — it is a placeholder replaced by a Kustomize replacement reading the encrypted argocd-repo-url-public secret. Every Application in this directory uses it.

  • Step 7: Register the Application

In apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml, insert - 62-td-sync.yaml between the 60-semaphore.yaml and 64-downloader-lidarr.yaml lines (around line 53):

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
sed -i 's|^  - 64-downloader-lidarr.yaml$|  - 62-td-sync.yaml\n  - 64-downloader-lidarr.yaml|' \
  apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml
grep -n -B1 -A1 '62-td-sync' apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml

Expected: 62-td-sync.yaml sitting between 60-semaphore.yaml and 64-downloader-lidarr.yaml.

  • Step 8: Validate before committing
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
kustomize build apps/td-sync --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec

Expected: Namespace, ServiceAccount, Deployment, Service, PVC, two CiliumNetworkPolicies and the Ingress, all carrying argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "62".

Then the schema check:

scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh apps/td-sync apps/argo-cd-apps

Expected: no failures. CiliumNetworkPolicy schemas come from the CRDs-catalog; if they are reported as skipped that is expected (-ignore-missing-schemas).

Then the full hook suite:

pre-commit run --all-files
  • Step 9: Commit and push
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
git add apps/td-sync apps/argo-cd-apps/62-td-sync.yaml apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml
git commit -m "feat(td-sync): deploy the td sync server on the internal ingress

Single-replica deployment on a Longhorn PVC, reachable only via
td.internal.neese-web.de. No Authelia middleware: the td CLI uses bearer
tokens and cannot follow an SSO redirect. Signup stays open until the first
account exists.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JTJMgDKXYPLzeS5Z7wFtgS"
git pull --rebase origin main
git push origin main
  • Step 10: Verify the rollout

ArgoCD polls; do not wait passively for more than a couple of minutes.

kubectl annotate -n argocd application 99-argocd-apps argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=hard --overwrite
sleep 30
kubectl get application -n argocd 62-td-sync \
  -o jsonpath='SYNC={.status.sync.status} HEALTH={.status.health.status}{"\n"}'

Expected: SYNC=Synced HEALTH=Healthy.

"Synced" alone does not prove your commit was applied — ArgoCD may be reporting against a stale revision. Confirm the revision:

kubectl get application -n argocd 62-td-sync -o jsonpath='{.status.sync.revision}{"\n"}'
git rev-parse HEAD

These must match. If not, re-annotate with refresh=hard and check again.

Then the pod:

kubectl get pods -n td-sync
kubectl logs -n td-sync deploy/td-sync --tail=30

Expected: one Running pod, 1/1 ready. The log should show Litestream starting and td-sync listening on :8080.

Then the TLS certificate. The ingress references wildcard-cloudflare-production-02, which is not created by this app — Reflector copies it from the certmanager namespace into every namespace, and a brand-new namespace gets it only after Reflector notices:

kubectl get secret -n td-sync wildcard-cloudflare-production-02 \
  -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.reflector\.v1\.k8s\.emberstack\.com/reflects}{"\n"}'

Expected: certmanager/wildcard-cloudflare-production-02.

If the secret is missing, wait a minute and retry — Reflector is eventually consistent. A persistently missing secret makes Traefik serve its default self-signed certificate, which looks like a certificate problem but is really a reflection problem.

  • Step 11: Verify the endpoint end to end
curl -sS https://td.internal.neese-web.de/healthz

Expected: {"status":"ok"}

If DNS does not resolve, the internal wildcard is not served to this host — that is a resolver question, not a manifest bug. Confirm the service itself is fine before chasing it:

kubectl run td-sync-check --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl:latest -n td-sync -- \
  curl -sS http://td-sync.td-sync.svc.cluster.local:8080/healthz

docs.title: Task 5: First account and closing signup
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: apps/td-sync/k8s.td-sync.yaml (the SYNC_ALLOW_SIGNUP value)

Interfaces: - Consumes: the running service from Task 4. - Produces: credentials in ~/.config/td/auth.json; a server with signup disabled.

  • Step 1: Point the CLI at the server
td config set sync.url https://td.internal.neese-web.de
  • Step 2: Start the login
td auth login

Enter the email address when prompted. The command blocks and polls — leave it running and use a second terminal for the next step. No code appears in the terminal; the login completes only after the emailed link is opened.

  • Step 3: Retrieve the verification link from the pod log

SYNC_EMAIL_PROVIDER=log writes the mail to stdout instead of sending it.

kubectl logs -n td-sync deploy/td-sync --tail=100 | grep -iE 'verify|login|token|http'

Open the printed URL in a browser on the internal network. Links expire after 15 minutes; if it has lapsed, re-run td auth login.

  • Step 4: Confirm the login completed

The td auth login terminal should report success. Verify:

test -f ~/.config/td/auth.json && echo "credentials stored"
  • Step 5: Close signup
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
sed -i '/name: SYNC_ALLOW_SIGNUP/{n;s/value: "true"/value: "false"/}' apps/td-sync/k8s.td-sync.yaml
grep -A1 'SYNC_ALLOW_SIGNUP' apps/td-sync/k8s.td-sync.yaml

Expected: value: "false".

Also update the stale comment above it:

sed -i 's|# Flipped to "false" in Task 5 once the first account exists.|# Signup is closed; the only account was created during rollout.|' \
  apps/td-sync/k8s.td-sync.yaml
  • Step 6: Validate, commit and push
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh apps/td-sync
git add apps/td-sync/k8s.td-sync.yaml
git commit -m "feat(td-sync): disable public signup

The single account exists; leaving registration open serves no purpose.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JTJMgDKXYPLzeS5Z7wFtgS"
git pull --rebase origin main
git push origin main
  • Step 7: Verify signup is actually closed

Wait for the sync, then confirm the pod restarted with the new value:

kubectl annotate -n argocd application 62-td-sync argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=hard --overwrite
sleep 30
kubectl get deploy -n td-sync td-sync \
  -o jsonpath='{range .spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[?(@.name=="SYNC_ALLOW_SIGNUP")]}{.value}{"\n"}{end}'

Expected: false.

docs.title: Task 6: Verify migration, then connect the real projects
docs.text:
The spec flags this as genuinely unknown: it is not documented whether td sync-project create uploads existing local history or only replicates events from that point on. Find out on throwaway data before risking the real backlog.

Files: none in either repo. This task produces knowledge and connected projects.

Interfaces: - Consumes: the authenticated CLI from Task 5. - Produces: a documented answer about history migration, and sync-connected projects.

  • Step 1: Back up the existing local state first
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
tar czf ~/todos-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz .todos/
ls -la ~/todos-backup-*.tar.gz

.todos/ is gitignored, so git is not a safety net here.

  • Step 2: Create a throwaway project with known history
mkdir -p /tmp/claude-1000/td-sync-migration-test
cd /tmp/claude-1000/td-sync-migration-test
td init
td create "Migration probe one" --type chore --priority P3
td create "Migration probe two" --type chore --priority P3
td log -i "$(td list --json | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)[0]["id"])')" "a log line written before any sync"
td list

Note the two issue IDs and confirm the log line is attached.

  • Step 3: Connect it and sync
cd /tmp/claude-1000/td-sync-migration-test
td sync-project create "migration-probe"
td sync
  • Step 4: Check whether the pre-existing history arrived

Pull into a clean checkout:

mkdir -p /tmp/claude-1000/td-sync-migration-verify
cd /tmp/claude-1000/td-sync-migration-verify
td init
td sync-project join   # select "migration-probe"
td sync
td list

Two possible outcomes, both actionable:

Result Meaning What to do Both issues and the pre-sync log line appear Full history is uploaded Connect the real projects directly in Step 5 Issues missing, or present without the pre-sync log line Only post-connection events replicate Stop. Report to the user before touching real projects — connecting them would leave the backlog server-side invisible

Record the outcome:

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
td log -i td-02c66e --decision "Migration probe result: <full history uploaded | only new events replicate>"
  • Step 5: Connect the real projects (only if Step 4 showed full history)
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
td sync-project create "k3s-git-ops"
td sync
td list

Confirm the issue count matches what td list showed before the sync.

  • Step 6: Clean up the probe
: > /tmp/claude-1000/td-sync-migration-test/.todos/README 2>/dev/null || true

Leave the server-side migration-probe project in place — it costs nothing and is useful for testing future upgrades.

docs.title: Task 7: Backup CronJob
docs.text:
Files: - Create: apps/td-sync/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml - Create: apps/td-sync/backup-env-configuration-td-sync.enc.yaml - Modify: apps/td-sync/kustomization.yaml - Modify: apps/td-sync/kustomize-secret-generator.yaml

Interfaces: - Consumes: PVC longhorn-pvc-td-sync and the pod label app.kubernetes.io/name: td-sync from Task 4; the td-sync image (for its sqlite3 binary). - Produces: restic snapshots tagged td-sync in the shared repository.

Why an initContainer: a plain restic backup over /data reads foo.db, foo.db-wal and foo.db-shm sequentially, not atomically. A concurrent write yields a torn, unrestorable snapshot. The initContainer produces consistent copies with sqlite3 .backup into an emptyDir, and restic ships only that — mirroring the existing MariaDB job, where an initContainer dumps and restic ships the dump.

  • Step 1: Create the restic env secret from an existing one

The repository credentials, ntfy settings and pushgateway URL are identical across all backup jobs. Copy an existing secret and change only the four job-specific fields. Never retype the shared values.

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/monitoring/backup-grafana-secrets.enc.yaml > /tmp/td-sync-backup.enc.yaml

Now edit /tmp/td-sync-backup.enc.yaml with the Read and Edit tools (Read is permitted under /tmp/**) and change exactly these five values, leaving RESTIC_REPOSITORY, RESTIC_PASSWORD, NTFY_* and PUSHGATEWAY_* untouched:

Field New value metadata.name backup-env-configuration-td-sync metadata.namespace td-sync RESTIC_SOURCE /backup/td-sync RESTIC_HOSTNAME td-sync RESTIC_ADDITIONAL_BACKUP_PARAMETERS --tag td-sync

Keep the kustomize.config.k8s.io/needs-hash: "true" annotation.

The grafana job excludes lost+found because it backs up a PVC root. Ours backs up an emptyDir, so no exclude is needed.

Then encrypt into place and wipe the plaintext:

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
sops --config .sops.yaml -e /tmp/td-sync-backup.enc.yaml > apps/td-sync/backup-env-configuration-td-sync.enc.yaml
: > /tmp/td-sync-backup.enc.yaml

Verify it decrypts and that no secret leaked into the repo in plaintext:

sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/td-sync/backup-env-configuration-td-sync.enc.yaml \
  | grep -E 'name:|namespace:|RESTIC_SOURCE|RESTIC_HOSTNAME|RESTIC_ADDITIONAL'
grep -c 'stringData' apps/td-sync/backup-env-configuration-td-sync.enc.yaml

Expected: the six lines above with the new values, and 1 for the second command with the values below it unreadable.

  • Step 2: Write the CronJob

apps/td-sync/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml:

---
# Hourly td-sync backup via restic.
#
# Co-located with the td-sync pod via podAffinity because the underlying
# Longhorn PVC is ReadWriteOnce - both pods must run on the same node.
#
# The PVC is mounted read-write, unlike the Grafana job: sqlite3 needs write
# access to the -shm file when opening a WAL database, so a read-only mount
# fails.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: backup-td-sync
  namespace: td-sync
spec:
  # :35 to stay clear of the Grafana job at :20.
  schedule: "35 * * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 3600
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 2
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 540
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app.kubernetes.io/name: backup-td-sync
            app.kubernetes.io/component: backup
        spec:
          automountServiceAccountToken: false
          restartPolicy: Never
          # Match td-sync's UID/GID so both the sqlite snapshot and restic can
          # read the volume without privilege escalation.
          securityContext:
            runAsUser: 1000
            runAsGroup: 1000
            fsGroup: 1000
            runAsNonRoot: true
          affinity:
            podAffinity:
              requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
                - labelSelector:
                    matchLabels:
                      app.kubernetes.io/name: td-sync
                  namespaces:
                    - td-sync
                  topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          initContainers:
            # Produce consistent copies of every SQLite database. Copying the
            # live db/-wal/-shm triplet with restic is not atomic and can yield
            # an unrestorable snapshot.
            - name: sqlite-snapshot
              image: forge.geekbundle.org/madic/td-sync:v0.65.0@sha256:REPLACE_WITH_DIGEST_FROM_TASK_2
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - |
                  set -eu
                  mkdir -p /snapshot/projects
                  echo "$(date) snapshotting server.db"
                  sqlite3 /data/server.db ".backup '/snapshot/server.db'"
                  for db in /data/projects/*.db; do
                    [ -e "$db" ] || continue
                    name=$(basename "$db")
                    echo "$(date) snapshotting projects/$name"
                    sqlite3 "$db" ".backup '/snapshot/projects/$name'"
                  done
                  echo "$(date) snapshot complete"
                  ls -la /snapshot /snapshot/projects
              volumeMounts:
                - name: td-sync
                  mountPath: /data
                  subPath: data
                - name: snapshot
                  mountPath: /snapshot
              securityContext:
                allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                capabilities:
                  drop:
                    - ALL
                privileged: false
          containers:
            - name: restic
              image: ghcr.io/madic-creates/container-restic:latest@sha256:5882ed8d36b4381ee2e6a7dad1a0c99f0341653a262209d655c69cee89770e62
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - /usr/local/bin/backup.sh
              env:
                # Give restic a writable HOME so it can keep its repo cache
                # under $HOME/.cache/restic between runs.
                - name: HOME
                  value: /home/restic
              envFrom:
                - secretRef:
                    name: backup-env-configuration-td-sync
              volumeMounts:
                - name: backup-script
                  mountPath: /usr/local/bin/backup.sh
                  subPath: backup.sh
                - name: snapshot
                  mountPath: /backup/td-sync
                  readOnly: true
                - name: home
                  mountPath: /home/restic
              securityContext:
                allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                capabilities:
                  drop:
                    - ALL
                privileged: false
          volumes:
            - name: td-sync
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: longhorn-pvc-td-sync
            - name: snapshot
              emptyDir:
                sizeLimit: 2Gi
            # Mirrored into every namespace by Reflector; the source ConfigMap
            # lives in the longhorn namespace.
            - name: backup-script
              configMap:
                name: crontab-backup-script
            - name: home
              emptyDir:
                medium: Memory
                sizeLimit: 200Mi
---
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: backup-td-sync
  namespace: td-sync
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: backup-td-sync
  egress:
    # DNS
    - toEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.cilium.k8s.namespace.labels.kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: kube-system
            k8s:k8s-app: kube-dns
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "53"
              protocol: UDP
            - port: "53"
              protocol: TCP
    # Prometheus Pushgateway (metrics)
    - toEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.cilium.k8s.namespace.labels.kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: monitoring
            k8s:app.kubernetes.io/name: prometheus-pushgateway
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "9091"
              protocol: TCP
    # Local restic REST-server (primary backup target)
    - toEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.cilium.k8s.namespace.labels.kubernetes.io/metadata.name: backup
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: backup
            k8s:app.kubernetes.io/name: rest-server
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "8000"
              protocol: TCP
    # ntfy notifications on failure (only HTTPS to the internet)
    - toEntities:
        - world
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "443"
              protocol: TCP

Replace REPLACE_WITH_DIGEST_FROM_TASK_2 with the same digest used in Task 4.

  • Step 3: Wire both new files into Kustomize

apps/td-sync/kustomization.yaml — add the CronJob to resources:

---
commonAnnotations:
  argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "62"

resources:
  - k8s.td-sync.yaml
  - k8s.pvc.yaml
  - k8s.np.td-sync-default-deny.yaml
  - k8s.np.td-sync.yaml
  - k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml

generators:
  - kustomize-secret-generator.yaml

apps/td-sync/kustomize-secret-generator.yaml — add the secret:

---
apiVersion: viaduct.ai/v1
kind: ksops
metadata:
  name: secret-generator
  annotations:
    config.kubernetes.io/function: |
      exec:
        path: ksops
files:
  - ingress.enc.yaml
  - backup-env-configuration-td-sync.enc.yaml
  • Step 4: Validate
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
kustomize build apps/td-sync --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec \
  | grep -E '^kind:|^  name:'

Expected to include kind: CronJob with name: backup-td-sync, and a kind: Secret whose name starts with backup-env-configuration-td-sync- followed by a hash suffix (from needs-hash: "true").

If the Secret name carries no hash suffix, the needs-hash annotation was lost while editing — go back to Step 1.

scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh apps/td-sync
pre-commit run --all-files
  • Step 5: Commit and push
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
git add apps/td-sync
git commit -m "feat(td-sync): back up the SQLite databases with restic

Litestream only replicates server.db; the per-project databases holding the
actual issues are not covered. An initContainer produces consistent sqlite
.backup copies before restic ships them, because copying a live WAL triplet
is not atomic.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JTJMgDKXYPLzeS5Z7wFtgS"
git pull --rebase origin main
git push origin main
  • Step 6: Trigger a run without waiting for the schedule

Creating a Job from a CronJob is not ArgoCD-managed, so this is allowed:

kubectl annotate -n argocd application 62-td-sync argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=hard --overwrite
sleep 30
kubectl get cronjob -n td-sync backup-td-sync
kubectl create job -n td-sync backup-td-sync-manual-01 --from=cronjob/backup-td-sync
  • Step 7: Verify both containers did their job
kubectl wait --for=condition=complete --timeout=300s -n td-sync job/backup-td-sync-manual-01
kubectl logs -n td-sync job/backup-td-sync-manual-01 -c sqlite-snapshot
kubectl logs -n td-sync job/backup-td-sync-manual-01 -c restic

Expected from sqlite-snapshot: snapshotting server.db, one line per project database, snapshot complete, and an ls listing showing non-zero file sizes.

Expected from restic: a completed restic backup with files added and a snapshot ID.

If sqlite-snapshot reports attempt to write a readonly database, the /data mount ended up read-only — check the volumeMount in Step 2.

  • Step 8: Confirm the snapshot is in the repository
kubectl logs -n td-sync job/backup-td-sync-manual-01 -c restic | grep -iE 'snapshot|processed|Added'

Expected: a snapshot ID and a non-zero count of processed files. A snapshot of zero files means the emptyDir was empty and the initContainer silently produced nothing — re-check Step 7.

docs.title: Task 8: Blackbox probe
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.enc.yaml

Interfaces: - Consumes: https://td.internal.neese-web.de/healthz from Task 4. - Produces: a probe_success timeseries for td-sync.

/metricz returns JSON rather than Prometheus exposition format and is deliberately not scraped. /healthz returns 500 when the database is unreachable, which is the signal worth alerting on.

  • Step 1: Regenerate the local values.yaml before touching anything

values.yaml is gitignored and generated from values.enc.yaml. A stale copy is the usual cause of confusing failures here — and apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.yaml currently exists as a 0-byte file, which the validation script will happily use instead of decrypting.

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.enc.yaml \
  > apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.yaml
wc -c apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.yaml

Expected: a few thousand bytes, not 0.

  • Step 2: Add the probe target

This is a structural edit to an encrypted file, so use Workflow B from CLAUDE.md.

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.enc.yaml \
  > /tmp/blackbox.enc.yaml

Edit /tmp/blackbox.enc.yaml with the Read and Edit tools. Under serviceMonitor.targets, append an entry after the last http-0N entry (currently http-06), before the cert-special-01 block:

        - name: http-07
          url: https://td.internal.neese-web.de/healthz

Two conventions of this file matter here:

  • Target names are deliberately generic. The file's own comment says so: only url and hostname are covered by the SOPS encrypted_regex, so a descriptive name: would sit in the repo in plaintext. Use the next free sequential number, not td-sync. (http-04 is absent; do not reuse it.)
  • Do not add a module key. serviceMonitor.defaults.module: http_2xx already applies, and that module handles the HTTPS handshake and follows redirects.

Then re-encrypt, regenerate the local values, and wipe the temp file:

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
sops --config .sops.yaml -e /tmp/blackbox.enc.yaml \
  > apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.enc.yaml
: > /tmp/blackbox.enc.yaml
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.enc.yaml \
  > apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.yaml
  • Step 3: Verify the target survived the round-trip
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.enc.yaml \
  | grep -A1 'name: http-07'
grep -c 'td.internal.neese-web.de' apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.enc.yaml

Expected: the http-07 target with its URL from the first command, and 0 from the second — the URL must be encrypted, not sitting in the repo in plaintext.

A SOPS MAC mismatch here usually means a comment ended up inside an encrypted sequence. Move any comment you added out of the targets list.

  • Step 4: Validate
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter
kustomize build apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec \
  | grep -c 'td.internal.neese-web.de'

Expected: validation passes and the grep returns a non-zero count — the ServiceMonitor for http-07 carries the URL as its target scrape parameter.

  • Step 5: Commit and push
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
git add apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/values.enc.yaml
git commit -m "feat(monitoring): probe td-sync health endpoint

/metricz returns JSON rather than Prometheus format, so /healthz via blackbox
is the useful signal - it returns 500 when the database is unreachable.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JTJMgDKXYPLzeS5Z7wFtgS"
git pull --rebase origin main
git push origin main

values.yaml is gitignored and must not appear in the commit — confirm with git status before pushing.

  • Step 6: Verify the probe is green
kubectl annotate -n argocd application 17-monitoring-blackbox-exporter argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=hard --overwrite
sleep 60
kubectl get servicemonitor -n monitoring | grep http-07

Then query Prometheus:

kubectl exec -n monitoring sts/prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus -c prometheus -- \
  wget -qO- 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/query?query=probe_success%7Binstance%3D~%22.*td.internal.*%22%7D'

Expected: a result with "value":[<timestamp>,"1"].

A value of 0 means the probe runs but the endpoint is unreachable from the monitoring namespace — check DNS resolution of the internal hostname from inside the cluster before blaming the manifest.

docs.title: Task 9: End-to-end verification of the update chain
docs.text:
The automation is the part most likely to be quietly broken, because nothing fails loudly when Renovate simply finds nothing. Prove the chain works while the context is fresh.

Files: none. This task produces evidence.

Interfaces: - Consumes: everything from Tasks 1-8.

  • Step 1: Confirm k3s-git-ops Renovate can see the image

The kubernetes manager is configured for /apps/.+/k8s\..*\.yaml$/, which matches apps/td-sync/k8s.td-sync.yaml. Confirm the reference has both a tag and a digest:

cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
grep -n 'td-sync:v' apps/td-sync/k8s.td-sync.yaml

Expected: two lines (Deployment and backup initContainer), both of the form forge.geekbundle.org/madic/td-sync:v0.65.0@sha256:....

A reference without :vX.Y.Z before the @ is the silent-failure case this whole design guards against.

  • Step 2: Confirm Renovate resolves the Forge registry anonymously
TOK=$(curl -s "https://forge.geekbundle.org/v2/token?scope=repository:madic/td-sync:pull&service=container_registry" \
      | sed -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" \
     "https://forge.geekbundle.org/v2/madic/td-sync/tags/list"

Expected: the tag list including v0.65.0. This is the same bearer-challenge flow Renovate's docker datasource performs.

  • Step 3: Trigger the k3s-git-ops Renovate manually

Run the Run renovatebot for updates workflow in madic-creates/k3s-git-ops via workflow_dispatch with dryRun: true and logLevel: debug.

Search the log for td-sync. Expected: the dependency is extracted with currentValue: v0.65.0 and a currentDigest. Whether an update is available does not matter — being found is the assertion.

If td-sync does not appear at all, the manager file pattern did not match. Re-check the filename is exactly k8s.td-sync.yaml.

  • Step 4: Record the verified state
cd /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/k3s-git-ops
td log -i td-02c66e "Update chain verified end to end: Renovate extracts marcus/td from docker-td's Dockerfile, Forge registry tag listing works anonymously, and k3s-git-ops Renovate extracts td-sync with tag+digest."
td handoff td-02c66e \
  --done "docker-td build repo (Dockerfile, build + renovate workflows, renovate.json5); apps/td-sync deployed via ArgoCD wave 62; first account created and signup closed; restic backup CronJob with sqlite snapshot initContainer; blackbox probe on /healthz; update chain verified" \
  --remaining "None for this scope" \
  --decision "See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-td-sync-server-design.md" \
  --uncertain "Whether the in-cluster forgejo-runner (65-forgejo-runner.yaml, commented out since 2025-12-15) should be removed from the repo as dead weight"
td review td-02c66e

docs.title: Notes for the reviewer
docs.text:
• The design spec is the reference. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-td-sync-server-design.md carries the reasoning behind every choice, including the three upstream findings that shaped it.
  • Three things were verified during design, not assumed: the Forge registry answers the anonymous bearer challenge; customManagers:dockerfileVersions matches the chosen ARG shape; td tags are clean semver.
  • Three things remain unverified until execution: the Forgejo Actions token has package-write; golang:1.27-alpine exists (Task 1 Step 1 checks this first); and whether td uploads pre-existing local history (Task 6 answers it before any real data is at risk).
  • The in-cluster forgejo-runner is disabled (apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml:59, commit 4a4bdc28, 2025-12-15). Builds run on a runner outside the cluster. Cleaning up that dead entry is out of scope here.

docs.title: llama.cpp on k3s with NVIDIA GPU — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-05-09 Status: Approved Author: Claude (brainstormed with @madic-creates)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Provide an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint inside the cluster, served by llama.cpp running on node04 (the ZFS node, which has an NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti / 8 GiB VRAM).

The endpoint must:

  • Serve a single fixed model (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, Q4_K_M GGUF) tuned for agentic / tool-calling workloads (large context, quantized KV cache, parallel serving slots).
  • Be reachable from the internal network at https://llama.internal.neese-web.de.
  • Authenticate every request with a shared API key (Bearer token).
  • Run on node04 only (nodeSelector: node-role/workload=zfs).
  • Use the GPU through the NVIDIA Kubernetes device plugin, with runtimeClassName: nvidia (the NVIDIA RuntimeClass already exists in the cluster).

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Multi-model serving / model swapping (would require llama-swap — out of scope, explicitly deferred).
  • Public exposure (cloudflare tunnel) — endpoint stays internal.
  • Authelia integration — API key is the only auth surface.
  • Replicas > 1 — there is exactly one consumer GPU.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Two new ArgoCD applications, deployed in dependency order via sync-waves:

Wave App Purpose 24 nvidia-device-plugin Advertise nvidia.com/gpu as a schedulable resource on every node carrying an NVIDIA GPU. 65 llama-cpp Run the inference server, consume nvidia.com/gpu: 1, expose Ingress.

Wave 24 matches the existing intel-gpu app — both are device plugins. Wave 65 places llama-cpp alongside other workload apps.

docs.title: Why a device plugin (and not just runtimeClass passthrough)
docs.text: The NVIDIA container toolkit alone (via runtimeClassName: nvidia) would let a pod see the GPU, but the scheduler would not know that the GPU is occupied. Two pods could land on the same node and fight over VRAM. The device plugin turns the GPU into a regular Kubernetes resource (nvidia.com/gpu), so the scheduler enforces single-tenancy.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
apps/nvidia-device-plugin/
  namespace.yaml
  kustomization.yaml
  k8s.np.nvidia-device-plugin-default-deny.yaml
  k8s.np.nvidia-device-plugin.yaml

docs.title: kustomization.yaml
docs.text:
Helm chart from the official NVIDIA repository:

helmCharts:
  - name: nvidia-device-plugin
    repo: https://nvidia.github.io/k8s-device-plugin
    version: <pinned, latest stable>
    namespace: nvidia-device-plugin
    releaseName: nvidia-device-plugin
    valuesInline:
      runtimeClassName: nvidia
      nodeSelector:
        feature.node.kubernetes.io/pci-0300_10de.present: "true"
      # Default behaviour is fine: one device per GPU, no MIG, no time-slicing.

The nodeSelector uses an existing NFD label (PCI vendor 10de = NVIDIA), so adding more NVIDIA nodes in the future requires no changes here.

runtimeClassName: nvidia is required because the device-plugin DaemonSet itself needs the NVIDIA runtime to talk to the driver.

docs.title: Network policies
docs.text:
• k8s.np.nvidia-device-plugin-default-deny.yaml — Cilium default-deny ingress + egress for namespace nvidia-device-plugin.
  • k8s.np.nvidia-device-plugin.yaml — allow only DNS egress + kubelet reachability. The plugin communicates with the kubelet over the device plugin Unix socket (/var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/), which is hostPath, not network — so very little egress is actually needed.

docs.title: ArgoCD Application
docs.text: apps/argo-cd-apps/24-nvidia-device-plugin.yaml, sync-wave "24", mirroring 24-intel-gpu.yaml. Add to apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml.

docs.title: Renovate
docs.text: Helm chart and image tags will be picked up by the existing Renovate manager config. Treat as a critical app like Longhorn/Traefik — add apps/nvidia-device-plugin/** to the automerge: false packageRules block in .github/renovate.json5 so that updates require manual review (a broken device plugin is cluster-wide).

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
apps/llama-cpp/
  namespace.yaml
  kustomization.yaml
  kustomize-secret-generator.yaml  # ksops config, references secrets.enc.yaml
  secrets.enc.yaml                 # SOPS-encrypted Secret manifest (input to ksops)
  k8s.deployment.yaml              # Deployment + Service
  llama-cpp.ingress.enc.yaml       # SOPS-encrypted (hostname matches encrypted_regex)
  k8s.np.llama-cpp-default-deny.yaml
  k8s.np.llama-cpp.yaml

docs.title: kustomization.yaml
docs.text:
resources:
  - namespace.yaml
  - k8s.deployment.yaml
  - llama-cpp.ingress.enc.yaml
  - k8s.np.llama-cpp-default-deny.yaml
  - k8s.np.llama-cpp.yaml

# ksops decrypts secrets.enc.yaml at build time and injects the Secret as if
# it were a regular resource. secrets.enc.yaml is NOT in `resources:`.
generators:
  - kustomize-secret-generator.yaml

commonAnnotations:
  argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "65"

docs.title: Deployment (k8s.deployment.yaml)
docs.text:
Plain Deployment + ClusterIP Service in one file (consistent with paperless-gpt).

Key fields:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: llama-cpp
  namespace: llama-cpp
spec:
  replicas: 1
  revisionHistoryLimit: 2
  strategy:
    type: Recreate          # GPU is single-tenant; rolling would deadlock.
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: llama-cpp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: llama-cpp
    spec:
      runtimeClassName: nvidia
      nodeSelector:
        node-role/workload: zfs
      containers:
        - name: llama-cpp
          image: ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-bXXXX  # pinned, Renovate-tracked
          args:
            - --model
            - /models/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf
            - --host
            - 0.0.0.0
            - --port
            - "8080"
            - --n-gpu-layers
            - "99"
            - --ctx-size
            - "32768"
            - --cache-type-k
            - q8_0
            - --cache-type-v
            - q8_0
            - --parallel
            - "1"
            - --flash-attn
            - --api-key-file
            - /etc/llama-cpp/api-key
            - --alias
            - qwen2.5-coder-7b
            - --jinja
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: http
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "2"
              memory: 8Gi
              nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            limits:
              cpu: "4"
              memory: 12Gi
              nvidia.com/gpu: 1
          volumeMounts:
            - name: models
              mountPath: /models
              readOnly: true
            - name: api-key
              mountPath: /etc/llama-cpp
              readOnly: true
      initContainers:
        # Fail fast with a clear error if the operator forgot to stage the
        # GGUF on node04, or if the file got truncated. Cheaper than a
        # CrashLoop on the main container, which buries the cause in
        # llama.cpp logs.
        - name: verify-model
          image: alpine:3.20
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              set -eu
              MODEL=/models/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf
              EXPECTED_SHA256=<pinned at implementation time>
              test -f "$MODEL" || { echo "model file missing: $MODEL"; exit 1; }
              # Quick sanity: GGUF magic is 'GGUF' (0x47475546) at offset 0
              head -c4 "$MODEL" | grep -q '^GGUF' || {
                echo "not a GGUF file (header mismatch)"; exit 1; }
              echo "$EXPECTED_SHA256  $MODEL" | sha256sum -c -
          volumeMounts:
            - name: models
              mountPath: /models
              readOnly: true
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: { path: /health, port: http }
            initialDelaySeconds: 30
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: { path: /health, port: http }
            initialDelaySeconds: 120  # model load can take a while on cold cache
            periodSeconds: 30
            failureThreshold: 6
      volumes:
        - name: models
          hostPath:
            path: /zfs/llama-cpp/models
            type: Directory
        - name: api-key
          secret:
            secretName: llama-cpp-env
            defaultMode: 0400
            items:
              - key: API_KEY
                path: api-key
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: llama-cpp
  namespace: llama-cpp
spec:
  selector:
    app: llama-cpp
  ports:
    - port: 8080
      targetPort: http
      protocol: TCP
  type: ClusterIP

docs.title: Ingress (llama-cpp.ingress.enc.yaml)
docs.text:
Plain networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, mirroring cluster-tv's pattern, but without Authelia forward-auth (auth happens at the API layer):

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: llama-cpp
  namespace: llama-cpp
  annotations:
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.entrypoints: web239,websecure239
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.tls: "true"
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.middlewares: traefik-redirect@kubernetescrd
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - llama.internal.neese-web.de
      secretName: wildcard-cloudflare-production-02
  rules:
    - host: llama.internal.neese-web.de
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: llama-cpp
                port:
                  number: 8080

The wildcard-cloudflare-production-02 TLS secret is the wildcard cert for *.internal.neese-web.de, reflected into namespaces by the existing reflector app.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Same pattern as paperless-gpt and other apps: a SOPS-encrypted Secret manifest plus a ksops generator that decrypts it during kustomize build.

apps/llama-cpp/secrets.enc.yaml (encrypted in the repo, the data: field matches the SOPS encryption regex):

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: llama-cpp-env
  namespace: llama-cpp
type: Opaque
stringData:
  API_KEY: <openssl rand -hex 32, generated once during Phase 2>

apps/llama-cpp/kustomize-secret-generator.yaml (plain text):

apiVersion: viaduct.ai/v1
kind: ksops
metadata:
  name: llama-cpp-secret-generator
  annotations:
    config.kubernetes.io/function: |
      exec:
        path: ksops
files:
  - secrets.enc.yaml

The kustomization.yaml references the ksops config under generators:, not under resources:. secrets.enc.yaml is not a resources: entry — ksops produces the Secret at build time.

docs.title: Network policies
docs.text:
• k8s.np.llama-cpp-default-deny.yaml — Cilium default-deny ingress + egress for namespace llama-cpp.
  • k8s.np.llama-cpp.yaml:
  • allow ingress from Traefik on port 8080
  • allow DNS egress (kube-system → kube-dns)
  • no other egress (the model is local; no internet access needed at runtime)

docs.title: ArgoCD Application
docs.text: apps/argo-cd-apps/65-llama-cpp.yaml, sync-wave "65", copied from 40-paperless-gpt.yaml pattern. Add to apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml.

docs.title: Manual Bootstrap (one-time, documented)
docs.text:
Before ArgoCD syncs llama-cpp, the model file must exist on node04:

ssh node04
sudo mkdir -p /zfs/llama-cpp/models
cd /zfs/llama-cpp/models
sudo huggingface-cli download bartowski/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-GGUF \
    Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf \
    --local-dir .
sudo chmod 644 *.gguf

If the file is missing, the pod will CrashLoopBackOff until it appears — ArgoCD will mark the app Degraded, which is the desired feedback.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After both apps reconcile:

# Device plugin advertises GPU
kubectl get node node04 -o jsonpath='{.status.allocatable.nvidia\.com/gpu}'
# expected: 1

# Pod is Running and Ready
kubectl get pod -n llama-cpp -l app=llama-cpp

# OpenAI endpoint replies with the loaded model
API_KEY=$(sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/llama-cpp/secrets.enc.yaml \
            | yq '.stringData.API_KEY')
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    https://llama.internal.neese-web.de/v1/models | jq

# Inference smoke test
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    https://llama.internal.neese-web.de/v1/chat/completions \
    -d '{"model":"qwen2.5-coder-7b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'

# Tool-calling smoke test (verifies --jinja path and OpenAI tools schema)
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    https://llama.internal.neese-web.de/v1/chat/completions \
    -d '{
      "model": "qwen2.5-coder-7b",
      "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"What is the weather in Berlin?"}],
      "tools": [{
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "get_weather",
          "description": "Get the current weather for a city",
          "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["city"]
          }
        }
      }]
    }' | jq '.choices[0].message.tool_calls'

docs.title: Placeholders to resolve at implementation time
docs.text:
• nvidia-device-plugin Helm chart version: — pin to current stable from https://nvidia.github.io/k8s-device-plugin
  • ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-bXXXX image tag — pin to current stable build (the project releases per-commit tags b<NNNN>).
  • API_KEY value — generated once via openssl rand -hex 32 during Phase 2 implementation.
  • EXPECTED_SHA256 in the verify-model initContainer — pin to the upstream-published SHA256 of the chosen GGUF file. Source of truth: https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-GGUF (the per-file checksum is shown next to each download). Compute locally with sha256sum after staging on node04 and confirm the values match before pinning.

docs.title: Risks and Open Questions
docs.text:
• VRAM budget on RTX 3060 Ti / 8 GiB.
  • Model (Q4_K_M of 7B): ~4.6 GiB
  • KV cache @ 32k context, q8_0 quantized, single slot: ~2 GiB
  • Compute buffers + flash-attn workspace: ~0.5–1 GiB
  • Total: ~7.0 GiB. ~1 GiB headroom. Monitor via nvidia-smi after deploy; if OOM under load, drop --ctx-size to 24576 (saves ~0.5 GiB) or move to Q3_K_M (saves another ~0.6 GiB).
  • Why Q4_K_M and not Q5_K_M. Agentic loops need long context for tool output history; the 0.9 GiB freed by Q4_K_M (vs Q5_K_M) is what makes 32k context feasible at all. Quality drop is small for code tasks.
  • --parallel 1 chosen deliberately. With --parallel >1, llama.cpp splits the configured context across slots, so the effective per-request context drops proportionally. The agentic use case prioritises long context per request over concurrency — there is exactly one human user anyway. Concurrency can be increased later if a real second consumer appears, at the cost of per-request context.
  • --flash-attn requires CUDA build (which we are using) and Compute Capability ≥ 7.0. RTX 3060 Ti is CC 8.6 — supported.
  • First request latency. Cold model load is ~10–20 s on this hardware. livenessProbe.initialDelaySeconds = 120 covers it.
  • Agentic limits. Qwen2.5-Coder-7B is decent at short tool-use loops (1–5 tool calls) but degrades on long-horizon agent sessions. For Aider/Cline-style work on large repos, expect to hit context limits or loops. Acceptable tradeoff for an 8 GiB card; revisit if a 16+ GiB GPU appears.
  • No backup of /zfs/llama-cpp/models. Acceptable: GGUF files are re-downloadable from HuggingFace and the path is on a ZFS dataset.
  • Renovate noise on llama.cpp image. The project tags every commit (e.g. b5821, b5822 …). Without throttling, this would produce many PRs. Mitigation: rely on the global minimumReleaseAge: '5 days', and consider adding apps/llama-cpp/** to the automerge: false rules so updates land with a manual click rather than auto-merge.

docs.title: Implementation Phases
docs.text:
To be expanded by writing-plans:

  1. Phase 1 — nvidia-device-plugin app: create files, encrypt nothing (no secrets), add ArgoCD Application, update kustomization, update Renovate rules, commit, let ArgoCD sync, verify nvidia.com/gpu: 1 is allocatable on node04.
  2. Phase 2 — llama-cpp app: create files, generate API key, encrypt secrets.enc.yaml and llama-cpp.ingress.enc.yaml, add ArgoCD Application, update kustomization. Before pushing: place the GGUF file on node04. Push, let ArgoCD sync, verify /v1/models and /v1/chat/completions.

docs.title: Downloader and unifi config volumes: hostPath → Longhorn PVC
Problem
docs.text:
Eight workloads keep their application config on the ZFS node via hostPath mounts:

App Namespace hostPath Size headphones downloader /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/headphones/config 41M lidarr downloader /vol_raidz1/container-scheduler/downloader-lidarr 165M nzbget downloader /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/nzbget/config 8.5M nzbget (scripts) downloader /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/nzbget/scripts 2.2M nzbhydra2 downloader /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/nzbhydra2/config 168M radarr downloader /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/radarr/config 1.2G radarr (trailer) downloader /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/Trailer-Downloader-Config 7K sonarr downloader /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/sonarr/config 299M trailarr downloader /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/trailarr/config 246M unifi-controller media /vol_raidz1/docker/configs/unify-controller/config 372M

None of these need to be hostPath. They should be regular PVCs so the data is managed by the cluster's storage layer instead of by directory layout on a single host.

Out of scope: the media trees (/vol_raidz1/{video,music,photo,downloads}) stay hostPath — they are bulk data served from ZFS and are not config.

unifi-controller is a late addition to this work. It is the same shape as the others — one config tree, one node — but it lives in namespace media and, unlike the *arr stack, it has no backup at all today. Since the migration turns its config into a Longhorn PVC, it also gets a restic CronJob modelled on Emby's, and joins the backup fleet's alerting and restore-test rotation.

docs.title: Current state
docs.text:
• All eight Deployments are pinned to node04 via nodeSelector: node-role/workload: zfs.
  • Longhorn runs on all four nodes, is the default StorageClass (3 replicas, Retain, volume expansion enabled). node04 has ~1.95 TB free.
  • apps/downloader/nzbget/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml mounts six of these config directories read-only via hostPath and backs them up hourly with restic. Its RESTIC_SOURCE (in backup-secrets.enc.yaml) lists the mount paths /backup/{sonarr,radarr,nzbget,nzbhydra2,trailarr,lidarr}.
  • headphones is intentionally not backed up.
  • apps/emby/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml is the reference pattern for backing up a Longhorn PVC: mount the PVC readOnly: true and co-locate the backup pod with the workload pod, because the volume is ReadWriteOnce.

docs.title: 1. PVCs
docs.text:
One k8s.pvc.yaml per app, added to that app's kustomization.yaml resources. Naming follows the existing convention (longhorn-pvc-nextpvr-config, longhorn-pvc-emby).

PVC Namespace Size longhorn-pvc-headphones-config downloader 2Gi longhorn-pvc-lidarr-config downloader 2Gi longhorn-pvc-nzbget-config downloader 1Gi longhorn-pvc-nzbget-scripts downloader 1Gi longhorn-pvc-nzbhydra2-config downloader 2Gi longhorn-pvc-radarr-config downloader 5Gi longhorn-pvc-radarr-trailer-downloader downloader 1Gi longhorn-pvc-sonarr-config downloader 2Gi longhorn-pvc-trailarr-config downloader 2Gi longhorn-pvc-unifi-controller-config media 5Gi

All: storageClassName: longhorn, accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce], volumeMode: Filesystem. Sizes leave headroom over current usage; Longhorn thin provisions, so real consumption is ~2.1 GB × 3 replicas.

PVCs carry no explicit sync-wave annotation of their own beyond whatever the app's commonAnnotations already sets. ArgoCD orders PersistentVolumeClaim before Deployment within a wave, so binding happens first either way.

docs.title: 2. Deployment changes
docs.text:
For each app:

  • The config volume changes from hostPath to persistentVolumeClaim. Container mount paths do not change.
  • Add strategy: {type: Recreate} where it is missing (headphones, nzbget, nzbhydra2, radarr, sonarr, unifi-controller). With a ReadWriteOnce volume a rolling update would let a second pod attach the same volume and write the same SQLite database. lidarr and trailarr already use Recreate.
  • nzbhydra2's /downloads mount becomes an emptyDir. The backing directory is empty (512 bytes) and is only scratch space.
  • radarr's trailer config keeps its current shape: PVC mounted with subPath: settings.ini at /opt/Trailer-Downloader/settings.ini, readOnly.
  • nzbget's scripts volume becomes a PVC, still mounted readOnly at /app/nzbget/scripts.
  • nodeSelector: node-role/workload: zfs stays on every Deployment. It is what keeps the RWO volumes attachable to one node and what co-locates the backup pod with the workloads.

Two of the eight would be free of host storage after the migration, and both keep the pin anyway for reasons that have nothing to do with this change:

  • nzbhydra2 mounts only its config PVC and an emptyDir. But its PVC is one of six mounted by the shared downloader backup CronJob, which is pinned to node04. If the nzbhydra2 pod moved, its ReadWriteOnce volume would attach on another node and the backup pod could no longer mount it — the whole downloader run would fail. Freeing it would mean splitting it into its own CronJob with podAffinity, which is out of scope here.
  • unifi-controller runs with hostNetwork: true. UniFi APs inform to a fixed host IP on ports the Service does not expose (8080, 3478/UDP, 10001/UDP), so a node change would silently orphan the APs. Its node binding comes from the network, not from storage, and the PVC does not change that.

docs.title: 3. Migration Jobs
docs.text:
One Job manifest per app in scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/<app>.yaml. This path is outside apps/, so no ArgoCD Application ever picks it up; the Jobs are applied by hand and deleted afterwards. They are never committed — they are throwaway artifacts that only need to exist in the working tree long enough to be applied once.

Job shape:

  • namespace downloader, nodeSelector: node-role/workload: zfs, restartPolicy: Never, backoffLimit: 2
  • busybox container, runAsUser: 0 (config trees are mixed-ownership: UID 0, 1000 and 1001)
  • mounts the old hostPath read-only at /src and the new PVC at /dst
  • nzbget and radarr each copy two volumes in one Job

Each copy step does, in order:

  1. Abort if /dst contains anything other than lost+found — protects against a second run overwriting already-migrated data.
  2. cp -a /src/. /dst/ — preserves ownership, modes and timestamps.
  3. Copy the source directory's own owner and mode onto the PVC root (stat -c '%u:%g' / %a from /src, then chown/chmod on /dst). A fresh Longhorn volume's root is root:root 0755; trailarr (UID 1000) and lidarr (UID 1001) need to be able to create files directly in /config.
  4. chmod 0755 /dst/lost+found. ext4 creates it as root:root 0700. The backup CronJob runs as UID 1000, and backup.sh uses set -eEu -o pipefail, so restic's exit code 3 on an unreadable directory would fail every backup run and fire an ntfy alert.

The downloader and media namespaces both have a default-deny CiliumNetworkPolicy. The Jobs need no network, so no policy change is required. The unifi-controller Job runs in media.

docs.title: 4. Backup CronJob changes
docs.text:
In apps/downloader/nzbget/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml, the six config hostPath volumes are replaced by the six corresponding PVCs, mounted readOnly: true.

  • Mount paths /backup/<app> stay identical, so the encrypted RESTIC_SOURCE needs no change.
  • securityContext stays runAsUser: 1000 / runAsGroup: 1002 / runAsNonRoot: true. Because cp -a preserves ownership and modes, the existing group-bit access argument still holds.
  • The existing nodeSelector already guarantees co-location with the workload pods, so no podAffinity is needed (Emby needs it only because Emby is not pinned to a node). A comment records the RWO dependency.
  • The header comment is updated: the volumes are no longer host filesystem paths.

docs.title: 4b. New backup CronJob for unifi-controller
docs.text:
unifi-controller has never been backed up. Now that its config is a Longhorn PVC, it gets a restic CronJob built to the same pattern as apps/emby/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml.

New file apps/unifi-controller/k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml holding a CronJob and a CiliumNetworkPolicy:

  • schedule 25 * * * * — the fleet is staggered per ten-minute slot and :25 is free (:00 paperless, :10 mariadb, :15 minecraft, :20 grafana, :30 emby, :40 nextpvr, :50 downloader)
  • podAffinity on app.kubernetes.io/name: unifi-controller with topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname, exactly as Emby does, because the PVC is ReadWriteOnce
  • the PVC mounted read-only at /backup/unifi-controller
  • securityContext: runAsUser: 1000 / runAsGroup: 1000 / runAsNonRoot: true — unifi-controller runs with PUID/PGID 1000 and every file under /config is owned by 1000:1000, so it does not need Emby's root treatment
  • home as a node-disk emptyDir with sizeLimit: 5Gi for restic's cache, with Emby's comment about why this is not a memory tmpfs
  • the CiliumNetworkPolicy mirrors Emby's: egress to kube-dns, the Pushgateway, the local rest-server, and world:443 for ntfy

New file apps/unifi-controller/backup-secrets.enc.yaml holding the backup-env-configuration-unifi Secret, SOPS-encrypted, with the same keys Emby's secret uses. Only three values differ from Emby's: RESTIC_SOURCE (/backup/unifi-controller), RESTIC_HOSTNAME (unifi) and the --tag unifi in RESTIC_ADDITIONAL_BACKUP_PARAMETERS. Repository, password, ntfy and Pushgateway settings are copied verbatim — the fleet shares one repository. The file is added to apps/unifi-controller/kustomize-secret-generator.yaml.

Joining the fleet also means three edits outside the app:

  • apps/backup-script/k8s.backup-alerts.yaml — add or absent(backup_start_timestamp{instance="unifi"}) to BackupNeverRun and name unifi in its description
  • apps/backup-script/k8s.restic-retentionpolicies.yaml — add unifi to the daily forget/prune tag loop. Every per-app secret sets RESTIC_RETENTION_POLICIES_ENABLED: "false" and defers pruning to this one job, so a missing tag means snapshots accumulate forever
  • apps/backup-script/k8s.restore-test.yaml — add unifi to TAGS and add a verifier branch checking $TARGET/backup/unifi-controller/data/system.properties, the file the controller writes for every site

docs.title: 5. Cutover
docs.text:
Two commits, with a manual step in between. All eight apps are down for the duration of the copy (~2.5 GB, a few minutes).

Commit A — prepare: - add the ten PVC manifests and wire them into the kustomizations - set replicas: 0 on all eight Deployments

ArgoCD syncs: pods terminate, PVCs are created and bind.

Manual step — run by the user (mutating kubectl is not available to the agent): 

kubectl apply -f scripts/migrate-hostpath-to-pvc/
kubectl -n downloader get jobs
kubectl -n media get jobs
kubectl -n <namespace> logs job/<name>
All eight Jobs must report success before continuing.

Commit B — cut over: - replicas: 1 on all eight Deployments - config volumes switched to the PVCs, strategy: Recreate added where missing - nzbhydra2 /downloads → emptyDir - downloader backup CronJob switched to PVCs - new unifi backup CronJob, its encrypted secret, the alert-rule and restore-test additions

After: - confirm each app starts and its UI shows the expected library/history - watch the next downloader backup run (:50) and the first unifi run (:25) and confirm both exit 0 - delete the migration Jobs - the old hostPath directories are left in place as a fallback and deleted manually after a few days

/vol_raidz1/docker/configs/downloader/lidarr/config (899M) is a stale leftover — the running lidarr uses /vol_raidz1/container-scheduler/downloader-lidarr. It is not touched by this work.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• kustomize build apps/downloader/<app> --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec succeeds for each changed app, and for apps/trailarr and apps/unifi-controller
  • sops --config .sops.yaml -d apps/unifi-controller/backup-secrets.enc.yaml decrypts and the rendered Secret is named backup-env-configuration-unifi
  • scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh passes for each changed app
  • pre-commit run --all-files passes
  • after Commit A: all ten PVCs Bound, all eight Deployments at 0 pods
  • after the Jobs: du -s on source and target agree per volume
  • after Commit B: all eight pods Running and Ready, apps reachable through their ingress, the downloader backup run exits 0, and the first unifi run produces a unifi snapshot (restic snapshots --tag unifi)

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Before Commit B nothing is lost — the hostPath data is untouched and reverting Commit A restores the previous state.

After Commit B, reverting the commit puts the Deployments back on the hostPath volumes; the hostPath data is still present but stale by however long the apps ran on the PVCs. Longhorn's Retain policy means the PVs survive a PVC delete, so the migrated data is recoverable either way.

docs.title: Design: Energy Dashboard (Household Consumption + PV Generation)
docs.text: Date: 2026-09-06 Issue: td-b80c1f

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
A Grafana dashboard showing household electricity consumption and photovoltaic generation together, so that current power flow, self-sufficiency and daily energy yield can be read at a glance.

Data sources:

  • FRITZ!Smart Energy 250 smart plug, read via the FRITZ!Box — reports signed power at the grid connection: positive while importing, negative while exporting PV surplus.
  • Deye SUN-M160G4-EU-Q0 micro inverter, read locally from its Solarman WiFi logger stick — reports current PV generation.

docs.title: Reconnaissance Findings (verified 2026-09-06)
docs.text:
These were measured against the live devices, not assumed:

  • Logger stick reachable at 192.168.1.136, TCP port 8899 open.
  • Stick status page (/status.html, basic auth admin/admin) reports inverter serial 2406160BE0, logger serial 3873566823, and live values (webdata_now_p, webdata_today_e, webdata_total_e).
  • Solarman V5 / Modbus works on this unit. Holding registers read successfully via pysolarmanv5:
  • 0x0056 = 3980 → 398.0 W AC active power (matches the status page)
  • 0x005B = 2462 → 246.2 V AC voltage
  • 0x005D = 4997 → 49.97 Hz grid frequency
  • 0x0075, 0x0076 = 458, 436 → DC string voltages This matters because public reports claim some 4th-generation Deye micro inverters ship with firmware that disables Modbus. This one does not.
  • The FRITZ!Box (192.168.1.1) initially offered only the users fritz7965 and Madic; the monitoring user referenced by the existing encrypted secret no longer existed. The operator has since recreated it, and the credentials now authenticate against the AHA interface.
  • The smart plug is a FRITZ!Smart Energy 250, AIN 16000 0036823 with the powermeter on sub-unit 16000 0036823-1. Live reading at the time of writing: 200 W draw, 241.3 V, lifetime counter 15 523 kWh — a lifetime counter that size confirms it meters the house rather than a single appliance.
  • The container image madic/fritzbox_exporter is not present on Docker Hub. The existing app (then at apps/prox01/fritzbox-exporter/, since moved) was commented out in apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml:59 and is not deployable as-is.

docs.title: Measurement Semantics
docs.text:
The FRITZ!Smart Energy plug measures grid draw, i.e. what is left after the PV generation has already been consumed. Therefore:

grid_import    = fritz_ha_multimeter_power_W      (measured)
generation     = deye_ac_active_power_w           (measured)
total_load     = grid_import + generation         (derived)
self_suff. [%] = generation / total_load * 100    (derived)

docs.title: Correction (2026-09-07): the plug is NOT direction-blind
docs.text:
This section previously claimed the plug measured magnitude only, so that exported surplus read as positive draw and inflated both total load and self-sufficiency. That was wrong and was never verified.

Measured over two days: 122 of 1672 samples are negative, minimum -202 W. The FRITZ!Smart Energy 250 reports signed power — negative while exporting.

Consequences:

  • total_load = grid + generation is correct in both directions after all, because the grid term carries the sign. No correction needed.
  • Self-sufficiency as generation / total_load overflows its own range: at 414 W generation against 396 W load it reads 105%, and up to 537% as load approaches zero. It is now capped with clamp_max(..., 1); whatever exceeds 100% is surplus, not self-sufficiency, and is reported separately by the surplus panels. The dashboard applies clamp_max a second time at query time, because a recording rule never rewrites the samples it already wrote — without that, the historical 105% and 537% readings would keep rendering.
  • Exported surplus is derived inline as clamp_min(-home:power_grid_import:watts, 0) rather than recorded as its own rule. A rule added later carries no history, and the surplus panels have to show past days.
  • Two power panels carried min: 0, silently clipping the exported half of the curve. Removed.
  • The "Plausibility check" row existed only to make invisible export visible. It survives as a plain unstacked overlay, where export is now directly readable as the area below zero.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Four new components across two ArgoCD applications.

Component Purpose Location pdreker/fritz_exporter TR-064 + AHA → fritz_ha_* metrics apps/monitoring-fritzbox-exporter/ (replaces the dead madic/ image) eclipse-mosquitto MQTT broker, cluster-internal only apps/solar/ kbialek/deye-inverter-mqtt Solarman V5 against 192.168.1.136:8899, metric group micro, protocol tcp apps/solar/ hikhvar/mqtt2prometheus MQTT topics → /metrics endpoint apps/solar/

docs.title: Why this data path
docs.text:
kbialek/deye-inverter-mqtt explicitly supports the M160 micro inverter (metric group micro) and is the best-maintained option, but publishes only to MQTT. Two alternatives were considered and rejected:

  • Custom Go exporter speaking Solarman V5 directly: one pod instead of three, but creates a permanently self-maintained component and image build for a niche protocol.
  • deye-inverter-mqtt plugin pushing to the existing Pushgateway: also one pod, but Pushgateway retains the last value indefinitely. For a live power dashboard, stale values silently presented as current is the worst available failure mode.

The chosen path costs two extra containers and keeps normal Prometheus pull semantics with no self-written code. The broker is reusable for future smart home integrations.

docs.title: Grouping
docs.text: The three solar components are deployed as a single ArgoCD application (apps/argo-cd-apps/66-solar.yaml, namespace solar, sync wave 66). None of them delivers value without the other two, so splitting them into separate applications would add ordering constraints without any benefit.

docs.title: Scraping
docs.text:
One ServiceMonitor per exporter. Because apps/monitoring/values.yaml:114 sets serviceMonitorSelectorNilUsesHelmValues: false, ServiceMonitors in any namespace are discovered without further Prometheus configuration.

Discovery is not reachability. The Prometheus CiliumNetworkPolicy carries a toEndpoints: - {} egress rule commented "scrape metrics from all namespaces", but in a namespaced CiliumNetworkPolicy an empty endpoint selector only matches endpoints in the policy's own namespace. Every scrape target outside monitoring therefore needs an explicit egress rule in apps/monitoring/k8s.np.monitoring.yaml — which is why a rule for databases/mariadb:9104 already exists there, and why one was added for solar/mqtt2prometheus:9641. The fritzbox exporter needs none: it runs in monitoring itself.

docs.title: Network policies
docs.text:
Following the repository's default-deny + per-app-allow Cilium pattern:

  • deye-inverter-mqtt: egress to 192.168.1.136:8899
  • fritz_exporter: egress to 192.168.1.1:49000 (TR-064) and :80 (AHA)
  • Both: ingress on the metrics port from Prometheus only
  • mosquitto: ingress from deye-inverter-mqtt and mqtt2prometheus only

docs.title: Polling
docs.text: Deye poll interval 30 s (upstream default is 60 s), Prometheus scrape interval 30 s. If the logger stick becomes unstable at that rate, fall back to 60 s.

docs.title: Manual Prerequisite
docs.text:
This cannot be automated and must be done by the operator before deployment:

  1. Create a FRITZ!Box user with the permissions "Smart-Home-Geräte steuern" and "FRITZ!Box-Einstellungen".
  2. Enable Heimnetz → Netzwerk → Netzwerkeinstellungen → Zugriff für Anwendungen zulassen (TR-064).
  3. Store username and password in the existing SOPS secret apps/monitoring-fritzbox-exporter/secrets.enc.yaml.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
From pdreker/fritz_exporter (verified in upstream source fritzexporter/fritzcapabilities.py, class HomeAutomation):

  • fritz_ha_multimeter_power_W — current power in W
  • fritz_ha_multimeter_energy_Wh — cumulative energy in Wh
  • fritz_ha_temperature_C, fritz_ha_device_present
  • Labels: serial, friendly_name, ain, device_name, device_id, manufacturer, productname

From the Deye chain. deye-inverter-mqtt publishes one MQTT topic per metric, so mqtt2prometheus is configured in metric_per_topic_config mode: the topic suffix is matched against mqtt_name and the raw payload is the value.

The topic list was read from the upstream sensor definitions (src/deye_sensors.py, entries carrying the micro group) rather than guessed. It yields 31 topics, of which 27 are mapped to 15 Prometheus metrics:

  • ac/active_power, ac/l1/{voltage,current}, ac/freq
  • day_energy, total_energy
  • radiator_temp, uptime, operating_power, dc/total_power
  • dc/pv{1..4}/{voltage,current,power,day_energy}
  • status (availability topic) → deye_logger_online

The four per-string total_energy topics are deliberately not mapped: lifetime per-string counters add series without answering a question the dashboard asks.

Per-string values share one metric name each and are distinguished by a string="pv1".."pv4" label, so a single panel can graph all four.

docs.title: Recording Rules
docs.text:
Derived values live in a PrometheusRule, not in dashboard expressions, so that every panel uses an identical definition:

  • home:power_grid_import:watts = sum(fritz_ha_multimeter_power_W)
  • home:power_generation:watts = sum(deye_ac_active_power_watts) or vector(0)
  • home:power_total:watts = grid import + generation
  • home:autarky:ratio = generation / clamp_min(total, 1)

or vector(0) on generation is load-bearing: the inverter powers down at night and its series disappear, which would otherwise make total household load vanish along with it.

Grid import is pinned to the plug's AIN (ain=~"16000.?0036823.*") so that a second smart plug paired later cannot be silently summed into household consumption. The regex is deliberately loose in two places: the FRITZ!Box lists the device both as 16000 0036823 and as the sub-unit 16000 0036823-1, and only the sub-unit carries the powermeter; the .? also absorbs the space in the AIN in case the exporter normalises it away. The same selector is applied to fritz_ha_multimeter_energy_Wh in the dashboard's daily bar chart.

The AIN is a local DECT device identifier, not a credential — it is useless without FRITZ!Box authentication — so it lives in plaintext alongside the LAN IPs the repository already publishes, rather than in a SOPS secret that a PrometheusRule could not read anyway.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
File: apps/monitoring/ks8.grafana-dashboards.energy.yaml (ConfigMap, label grafana_dashboard: "1", matching the existing dashboard pattern). Title: Energie — Verbrauch & PV. Default range 24 h, refresh 30 s.

Row 1 — Snapshot. Four stat panels: generation, grid import, total load, self-sufficiency. The four numbers the dashboard gets opened for.

Row 2 — Core chart. Stacked time series of grid import + generation. The stack height is total load and the yellow share is self-sufficiency, so both are readable without arithmetic. Below it, self-sufficiency in % as its own curve.

Row 3 — Energy rather than power. Yield today and total, plus a bar chart of PV kWh against grid-import kWh per day over 14 days (increase(fritz_ha_multimeter_energy_Wh[1d])). This answers "is it worth it", which the power curves cannot.

Row 4 — Plausibility check. Grid import and generation overlaid, not stacked. Where grid import rises together with PV output instead of falling, the export periods described under "Known limitation" become visible.

Row 5 — System health (collapsed by default). DC voltage and current per MPPT string (a shaded or failed panel shows up immediately), AC voltage and grid frequency (excessive grid voltage makes the inverter throttle — the most common explanation for unexpectedly low output), inverter temperature, and scrape status of both sources.

docs.title: Alerting
docs.text:
Three alerts, routed through the existing Alertmanager chain:

  • SolarExporterDown / FritzboxExporterDown: up == 0 for 10 min.
  • EnergyGridImportMissing: the pinned AIN matches nothing while the exporter is up, i.e. the plug was re-paired and the dashboard would silently show generation only.

The design originally called for a staleness alert on "no MQTT message received for 10 min".
