That was dropped: the inverter legitimately stops publishing every night, so it would have fired nightly. up == 0 on the exporter pod carries the same signal without the seasonal false positives, and the short mqtt2prometheus cache timeout (5 min) already prevents stale values from being served as current — the series simply disappears instead.

A "no production at midday" alert is deliberately omitted: without solar position data it is a winter-long noise source.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• kustomize build apps/solar --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec
  • scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh apps/solar and the same for the rewritten apps/monitoring-fritzbox-exporter
  • pre-commit run --all-files
  • Dashboard JSON validated by building the ConfigMap and confirming the Grafana sidecar loads it without error.
  • Post-deploy: confirm both /metrics endpoints return the expected series, and cross-check deye_ac_active_power_w against the logger stick's own status page.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Solarman cloud API integration (not needed — local access works).
  • Cost/tariff calculations.
  • Any write access to the inverter (read-only Modbus only).

docs.title: Design: Shelly Plug M Gen3 Integration (Per-Appliance Breakdown)
docs.text: Date: 2026-09-07 Issue: td-17eb5e Builds on: 2026-09-06-energy-dashboard-design.md

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Meter four individual appliances — mini server, washing machine, tumble dryer, fridge — with Shelly Plug M Gen3 smart plugs, and show them against total household consumption so it is visible which share of the household load is accounted for.

Status: blocked on hardware. The devices have not arrived. Nothing is implemented until the Gen3 compatibility check below passes on a real device.

docs.title: Device Facts (from vendor documentation, not assumed)
docs.text:
• Shelly Gen3 speaks the same RPC API as Gen2 (/rpc/Shelly.GetStatus).
  • Over MQTT, Gen2/Gen3 devices publish JSON objects on <topic_prefix>/status/switch:0. There is no mode that publishes one scalar per topic.

docs.title: Data Path
docs.text: webdevops/shelly-plug-exporter polls the four plugs over HTTP RPC and exposes /metrics; Prometheus scrapes the exporter.

docs.title: Why this and not MQTT
docs.text:
The Shellys can publish to MQTT natively and a broker already runs in the solar namespace, which looks like the cheaper path. It is not:

  • mosquitto currently accepts connections only from inside its namespace and runs anonymous — the CiliumNetworkPolicy is the entire access control. Letting four LAN devices publish into it means exposing the broker to the LAN and retrofitting authentication.
  • It reverses the data direction. Every other LAN integration here (FRITZ!Box, Deye logger) has the cluster pull from the device.
  • It needs a second mqtt2prometheus instance regardless: Shelly publishes JSON objects, the existing instance runs in metric_per_topic mode, and upstream config.go rejects a configuration that sets both object_per_topic_config and metric_per_topic_config.

MQTT stays the documented fallback if the exporter turns out not to support Gen3.

A third option — driving the exporter's /probe?target= endpoint with one ServiceMonitor per plug, mirroring monitoring-blackbox-exporter — was rejected as premature: it makes a single failed plug visible as its own up == 0, but costs four manifests and moves the appliance names into Git. Revisit if per-plug availability turns out to matter.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
New application apps/monitoring-shelly-exporter/, following apps/monitoring-fritzbox-exporter/ exactly:

File Purpose kustomization.yaml namespace monitoring, commonAnnotations sync-wave 17 k8s.deployment.yaml the exporter, static host list of the four plug IPs k8s.service.yaml ClusterIP on the metrics port k8s.servicemonitor.yaml scrape interval 30s k8s.np.shelly-exporter.yaml egress to the four plug IPs on 80; ingress from Prometheus only

Plus apps/argo-cd-apps/17-monitoring-shelly-exporter.yaml with metadata.name: 17-monitoring-shelly-exporter, destination.namespace: default and no CreateNamespace, matching the sibling monitoring-* applications.

No Prometheus egress rule is needed: unlike solar/mqtt2prometheus, this exporter runs inside monitoring, which the policy's toEndpoints: - {} rule already covers.

docs.title: Manual Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Fixed IPs for all four plugs via DHCP reservation in the FRITZ!Box. Not optional — the Cilium policy matches CIDRs, so a changed lease silently breaks egress.
  2. Set the device name in each plug ("Waschmaschine", "Trockner", "Kühlschrank", "Mini-Server"). The exporter exposes it as the plugName label, so the dashboard gets readable names without hard-coding them in Git.
  3. Leave device authentication off. Gen3 ships with it disabled, and the plugs are reachable by anything on the LAN regardless; the policy protects the cluster→device direction. If it is enabled later, credentials go into a SOPS secret alongside the app.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
From the exporter (label set verified in upstream shellyplug/metrics.go: target, mac, plugName, plus id and name on the power/switch/temp series):

  • shellyplug_power_load_current — current power in W
  • shellyplug_power_load_total — cumulative energy in Wh
  • shellyplug_switch_on, shellyplug_temperature — device health
  • shellyplug_info — carries plugModel, plugGeneration, hostname

Every dashboard query aggregates the infrastructure labels away, as max by (plugName) (...). A pod restart otherwise creates a second series per plug and each panel renders it twice — this happened on the energy dashboard and is the reason the rule is written down here.

docs.title: Recording Rules
docs.text:
Added to apps/monitoring/k8s.prometheusrule.energy.yaml:

  • home:power_measured:watts = sum(shellyplug_power_load_current)
  • home:power_unaccounted:watts = clamp_min(home:power_total:watts - home:power_measured:watts, 0)

clamp_min is load-bearing: the plugs and the FRITZ meter are sampled independently, so timing offsets produce briefly negative differences without it.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
A new "Geräte" row in the existing Energie — Verbrauch & PV dashboard rather than a separate one — the comparison against total consumption is the whole point, and it only reads directly if it sits next to the totals.

  1. Stacked time series: the four appliances plus "Rest (nicht gemessen)". The stack height is total household consumption, so the unexplained share is readable without arithmetic. A timeseries panel handles the five frames; see the note under 2 for why Bar chart cannot.
  2. Energy per appliance per day (kWh) from increase(shellyplug_power_load_total[1d]), with the same midnight-aligned 1d step as the PV panel. Two consequences carried over from building that panel, both of which cost a debugging round there: - It produces no bar until a full day boundary has passed. Grafana aligns range-query start and end down to multiples of the step, so with a 1d step every evaluation point is a midnight. - Use a timeseries panel with custom.drawStyle: "bars", not the Bar chart panel. Bar chart supports only one dataset ("using multiple datasets can result in unexpected behavior" — Grafana docs), and four appliances means four data frames, which renders as an empty panel.
  3. Four stat tiles with current power per appliance.

Colours: five series (four appliances plus the remainder) need a palette run through dataviz's validator for both light and dark, as was done for the generation/import pair.

docs.title: The remainder is sound
docs.text: An earlier draft warned that the remainder would inherit "export blindness" from the FRITZ plug. That premise was wrong: the plug reports signed power, so home:power_total:watts is the true household load in both directions and the remainder needs no caveat. See the correction section in the energy dashboard spec.

docs.title: Alerting
docs.text:
up == 0 on the exporter for 10 minutes. Nothing per appliance.

A "fridge has drawn 0 W for hours" alert would be genuinely useful — it catches a failed appliance — but defrost and compressor cycles make the threshold guesswork without data. Design it separately after a few weeks of history.

docs.title: Open Questions to Resolve Before Implementing
docs.text:
1. Does the exporter read a Gen3 device at all? It advertises generation 1 and 2. Check by pointing it at one plug and confirming shellyplug_info reports plugGeneration="3" with a non-zero shellyplug_power_load_current. If it fails, fall back to the MQTT path.
  2. Which host flag applies? The exporter has separate --shelly.host.shellyplug, --shelly.host.shellyplus and --shelly.host.shellypro options and it is not obvious which covers a Plug M Gen3. Determine empirically; do not guess.
  3. Image tag. Pin a concrete released tag from the upstream registry at implementation time; do not use latest.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• kustomize build apps/monitoring-shelly-exporter --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec
  • scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh apps/monitoring-shelly-exporter apps/monitoring
  • promtool check rules on the extended PrometheusRule, and the dashboard expressions extracted into a synthetic rules file, as before.
  • Post-deploy: confirm four distinct plugName values appear and that home:power_measured:watts is plausible against home:power_total:watts.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Switching the plugs on or off from the cluster. Read-only.
  • Per-appliance anomaly alerting.
  • Replacing the FRITZ!Smart Energy as the grid-import meter.

docs.title: Addendum, 2026-09-11: eleven plugs
docs.text:
Seven more Shelly Plug M Gen3 joined the four: Spuelmaschine (.91), Kuehlschrank (.89), Router (.189), Arbeitsplatz 1 (.66), Arbeitsplatz 2 (.173), Wohn Fernseher (.108), Wohn Verstaerker (.150). Same model and firmware (2.0.0) as the existing plugs, and the exporter's shared password is accepted, so no secret changed.

Personal names stay out of Git. Two plugs carry first names on the device. In the repository they are only "Arbeitsplatz 1" and "Arbeitsplatz 2"; the real name reaches Grafana at runtime through the name label. Consequently no panel or rule may match a plug by name.

Identity is the MAC. Plugs are selected into groups by address (the same IPs as the host list and the egress policy) and aggregated by mac. name was the identity before and failed: the fourth plug was renamed from "Kuehlschrank" to "Tiefkuehlschrank" on 2026-09-11, and the next plug to arrive was a real fridge called "Kuehlschrank", so by name the freezer's first hours merged into the fridge. home:power_measured:watts and ShellyExporterDeviceMissing were moved to by (mac) for the same reason; the alert threshold is now 11.

Four groups, not eleven colours. The categorical palette has eight validated slots, four already carry fixed meanings, and under the all-pairs check that a stacked chart requires even the full eight fail (CVD dE 1.6, normal-vision dE 7.1). The stacked power chart and the daily energy bars therefore show four groups by load profile -- Waschen & Spuelen, Wohnzimmer, Kuehlen, IT & Netz -- in the four passing slots, and each plug appears as a labelled bar whose colour marks its group. The operator chose this over per-plug small multiples. Grouping by load profile rather than room keeps the continuous loads -- Kuehlen, IT & Netz -- readable as the bulk of base load.

docs.title: Design: Solar Irradiance as an Expected-Yield Reference
docs.text: Date: 2026-09-07 Issue: td-40206d Builds on: 2026-09-06-energy-dashboard-design.md Related: 2026-09-07-shelly-plugs-design.md (td-17eb5e)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Give the energy dashboard a reference for what the PV array should be producing, so that a given output figure can be judged instead of merely read. 250 W at 15:00 is either an overcast afternoon or a failing array, and today nothing distinguishes the two.

Per-string DC values already catch relative faults — pv1 diverging from pv2. They cannot catch a fault that affects both strings equally: soiling, snow, curtailment, gradual degradation. An external irradiance reference supplies the missing "what should it be doing".

docs.title: Scope Decision
docs.text:
Reference only. Open-Meteo also serves a forecast, and an hourly forecast would make load shifting actionable — the measured surplus of 0.15 kWh against 3.1 kWh generated says the lever for self-consumption is running the washing machine while the sun is up, not producing more.

That is deliberately out of scope here. Prometheus stores what has happened; future-timestamped samples do not belong in it, so a forecast panel would need a second Grafana datasource (Infinity/JSON-API), a new plugin, and a new egress path — roughly doubling the surface area of a P3 issue. It becomes a follow-up once td-17eb5e's plugs exist to act on it.

No standalone sunshine panel. The inverter already measures irradiance at the panels directly via per-string DC voltage and current; external data is a proxy for that. It earns its place only through expected-vs-actual comparison.

docs.title: Site Parameters
docs.text:
Supplied by the operator, converted to Open-Meteo's convention (0 = south, negative = east, positive = west; the operator gave compass bearings, where 0 = north).

String Compass bearing Open-Meteo azimuth Tilt Peak power pv1 45° (NE) -135 40° 560 Wp pv2 225° (SW) +45 40° 560 Wp

Total 1120 Wp into a Deye SUN-M160G4. pv3 and pv4 are not connected and always read 0 — correct, not a fault.

Tilt, azimuth and peak power are not location-identifying and stay in plain YAML. The site coordinates are handled separately — see "Location Privacy".

The near-opposite orientation of the two strings is the central fact of this design. A single averaged tilt/azimuth would misrepresent both panels: the NE string peaks late morning, the SW string mid-afternoon. Each string needs its own irradiance series.

docs.title: Verified API Behaviour
docs.text:
Every statement below was executed against api.open-meteo.com on 2026-09-07 with the real site coordinates. No API key is required.

One tilt/azimuth pair per request. Passing comma-separated values with duplicated coordinates fails:

HTTP 400  {"error":true,"reason":"Value was not of type 'Float' at path 'tilt'."}

Two orientations therefore mean two requests.

current= is supported and returns 15-minute values. This is what makes the exporter simple — no indexing into an hourly array, no timezone arithmetic:

"current_units":{"time":"iso8601","interval":"seconds","global_tilted_irradiance":"W/m²"},
"current":{"time":"2026-09-07T17:15","interval":900,
           "global_tilted_irradiance":468.5,"shortwave_radiation":320.0,"cloud_cover":18}

The native interval is 900 s, so polling faster than every 15 minutes gains nothing.

The grid cell is not the exact site. Open-Meteo snaps the request to its own model grid, which resolved roughly 1 km from the site (elevation 64 m). Acceptable for an irradiance reference; worth knowing before chasing a small systematic offset. It also means sub-kilometre precision in the stored coordinates buys nothing.

GTI already incorporates cloud cover. Measured today: 448 W/m² at 4% cloud at midday, against heavily suppressed morning values at 100% cloud. This is the property that makes the whole design work — see "Why the ratio is a health signal" below.

docs.title: Modelled vs. actual, 2026-09-07
docs.text:
Hour NE GTI SW GTI Expected at PR=1.0 09:00 145.6 81.2 127 W 12:00 448.3 511.4 537 W 14:00 334.7 758.0 612 W 16:00 168.4 793.3 539 W 19:00 89.2 289.1 212 W

Ideal day total 4.56 kWh against roughly 3.1 kWh actually generated, giving a performance ratio of about 0.68 — a believable real-world figure for a fixed, steeply mounted split-orientation array.

The 3.1 kWh figure comes from an earlier session's log, not from a query run during this design: the calibration query against Prometheus was blocked by the sandbox because the endpoint document carries an inline credential. Confirming 0.68 against a clear day is an implementation step, not an established fact.

docs.title: Location Privacy
docs.text:
The site coordinates must never appear in plain text anywhere in this repository. They identify the operator's home address to within a few metres, and the repository is public.

They are therefore stored in apps/solar/secrets.enc.yaml, the SOPS-encrypted Secret that already exists in this app for the inverter serial number. Its stringData block matches the encrypted_regex for .*.enc.yaml in .sops.yaml, so two new keys are encrypted automatically with no config change:

stringData:
  serial_number: <existing>
  latitude: <encrypted>
  longitude: <encrypted>

The exporter reads them as environment variables via secretKeyRef (OPENMETEO_LATITUDE, OPENMETEO_LONGITUDE), exactly as monitoring-fritzbox-exporter reads its credentials.

Three consequences that are easy to get wrong:

  1. The exporter must not emit coordinates as metric labels. Open-Meteo echoes latitude/longitude in every response and the naive thing is to pass them through. A Prometheus label is readable by anyone with dashboard access and is copied into every backup of the TSDB.
  2. No coordinates in log output, including on error. Log the failing parameter names, never the query string.
  3. No coordinates in this spec, in commit messages, or in docs/energy-metrics-api.md — that file is handed to an external agent which needs the array geometry to reason about the generation curve but has no use for the location.

Because the model grid snaps to roughly a kilometre anyway, storing fewer decimal places costs no accuracy — but rounding is defence in depth, not a substitute for encryption.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
api.open-meteo.com
        │  2 × HTTPS GET every 15 min (one per string orientation)
        ▼
openmeteo-exporter          Deployment, namespace solar, sync wave 66
        │  /metrics, served from memory
        ▼
Prometheus                  ServiceMonitor
        │
        ▼
recording rules             namespace monitoring, energy.rules group
        │
        ▼
energy dashboard

docs.title: Why an exporter Deployment and not a CronJob to pushgateway
docs.text:
Pushgateway serves its last value forever. A dead CronJob would keep showing yesterday's irradiance as "expected now", making a healthy array look broken or a broken one look fine. That is the same reason pushgateway was rejected for the Deye inverter, and it is worse here: the entire purpose of this series is to judge health, so a stale reference is actively misleading rather than merely absent.

An exporter gets the right failure semantics for free — up == 0 alerts, and the series disappear with the pod instead of lying.

docs.title: Why a stock image with a mounted script, and not a built image
docs.text:
The exporter is ~50 lines of standard-library Python. Building and publishing a container image for that would add a release pipeline and one more thing for Renovate to track. apps/solar already has the pattern this needs: a configMapGenerator that appends a content hash to the ConfigMap name so a config change actually restarts the pod (used today for mosquitto.conf and the mqtt2prometheus config, both of which read their configuration only at startup).

The script uses standard library only — no pip install at container start, which would make the pod depend on a package index being reachable at boot.

docs.title: Why namespace solar and not monitoring
docs.text: It is a PV data source and belongs beside the inverter bridge it references. The rules and dashboard stay in monitoring with the rest of the energy logic.

docs.title: Metrics Contract
docs.text:
The exporter emits measurements and site configuration only — never derived quantities. No performance ratio, no expected watts. That keeps the model in git-tracked PromQL where changing it is a commit rather than a pod restart.

Metric Type Unit Notes solar_irradiance_tilted_wm2{string="pv1"\|"pv2"} gauge W/m² GTI at that string's orientation solar_irradiance_global_horizontal_wm2 gauge W/m² GHI, orientation-independent context solar_cloud_cover_ratio gauge 0..1 context solar_array_peak_power_watts{string=...} gauge W static 560 per string solar_openmeteo_last_success_timestamp_seconds gauge s staleness signal solar_openmeteo_request_failures_total counter

solar_array_peak_power_watts is exported rather than written as a literal in PromQL so the rules read as a formula over labelled data. Adding a third panel later becomes a config change, not a rule edit.

GHI and cloud cover are orientation-independent and are taken from the first of the two requests only.

docs.title: Serving details
docs.text: Metrics port 9779, named metrics. ServiceMonitor scrapes every 60 s with a 10 s timeout. The scrape is a pure in-memory read — it never triggers an API call — so the interval is free to be short and is unrelated to the 15-minute poll. A readinessProbe on the metrics port is an HTTP probe here, unlike fritzbox-exporter's deliberate TCP probe, precisely because serving costs nothing.

docs.title: Behaviour on API failure
docs.text: The last good values are kept in memory and continue to be served; solar_openmeteo_last_success_timestamp_seconds stops advancing and SolarIrradianceStale catches it. The exporter must not exit on a failed poll — a transient API error should not take the reference offline — but it must also not silently serve week-old data without saying so, which is what the timestamp metric is for.

docs.title: Recording Rules
docs.text:
Added to the existing energy.rules group in apps/monitoring/k8s.prometheusrule.energy.yaml.

Every raw metric is wrapped in max by (string), per that file's own documented rule about exporter pod restarts creating a new series per pod.

# PR = 1.0 physical ceiling
solar:ideal_power:watts =
  sum(
    max by (string) (solar_irradiance_tilted_wm2) / 1000
      * on (string) group_left max by (string) (solar_array_peak_power_watts)
  )

# The single performance-ratio literal in the whole design
solar:expected_power:watts = solar:ideal_power:watts * 0.68

solar:performance_ratio =
  home:power_generation:watts / clamp_min(solar:ideal_power:watts, 1)

clamp_min(..., 1) guards the division at night when the ceiling is zero.

The 0.68 carries a comment stating it was calibrated from one day (4.56 kWh modelled against ~3.1 kWh actual) and must be revisited after several clear days.

docs.title: Why the ratio is a health signal
docs.text: Because Open-Meteo's GTI already includes cloud cover, actual / ideal stays roughly flat across weather. A cloudy day lowers both the numerator and the denominator. A drop in the ratio therefore points at the array, not the sky — which is exactly the fault class the per-string DC values cannot catch.

docs.title: Alerting
docs.text:
SolarArrayUnderperforming
  solar:performance_ratio < 0.40 and solar:ideal_power:watts > 300
  for: 2h        severity: warning

SolarIrradianceExporterDown
  up{job="openmeteo-exporter"} == 0
  for: 30m       severity: warning

SolarIrradianceStale
  time() - solar_openmeteo_last_success_timestamp_seconds > 3600
  for: 30m       severity: warning

0.40 sits between the 0.68 baseline and the ~0.34 that losing one of two strings would produce. The ideal_power > 300 guard keeps dawn, dusk and deep overcast out of the comparison, where a small absolute error produces a wild ratio. for: 2h keeps passing weather out.

Both constants are provisional. They are derived from a single day, which is precisely the kind of unverified assumption the comments in k8s.prometheusrule.energy.yaml exist to warn about. They must be re-evaluated once a few weeks of solar:performance_ratio history exists, and the rule file must say so.

SolarIrradianceExporterDown uses up, not metric absence — consistent with SolarExporterDown and FritzboxExporterDown. Unlike the inverter, this exporter has no legitimate nightly outage, so a 30m window is safe.

The two staleness alerts are complementary and neither is redundant: ...ExporterDown catches a dead pod (at which point the timestamp metric is absent and cannot fire), while ...Stale catches the harder case of a healthy pod that has lost its upstream and is quietly serving old values.

docs.title: Network Policy
docs.text:
The exporter is the first internet-dependent source in the energy stack — every other one (inverter logger, FRITZ!Box) is LAN-local.

A new CiliumNetworkPolicy selecting only app.kubernetes.io/name: openmeteo-exporter:

  • ingress: Prometheus from monitoring, on the metrics port
  • egress: DNS to kube-dns, and HTTPS to api.open-meteo.com

docs.title: Known risk: toFQDNs may not be load-bearing in this cluster
docs.text:
Cilium's toFQDNs only works when the DNS request passes through Cilium's DNS proxy, which requires a toPorts rule carrying rules.dns.matchPattern on the DNS egress. No policy in this repository has such a rule. The existing toFQDNs entries (cert-manager, CoreDNS, pihole-01, pihole-03) may therefore never have been load-bearing — cert-manager's, for instance, is backstopped by a toCIDRSet covering the same addresses.

Plan: use toFQDNs together with a proper DNS-proxy rule, scoped to this exporter's endpoint only. Cilium policies apply per endpoint selector, so deye-inverter-mqtt and mqtt2prometheus keep their current DNS path untouched and cannot be broken by this change.

Fallback if egress does not come up: toEntities: world on port 443, the pattern proven in apps/epicgames-freegames. Broader than ideal for a pod that talks to exactly one API, but known to work. Verify with hubble observe --namespace solar before concluding either way.

docs.title: Dashboard Changes
docs.text:
apps/monitoring/ks8.grafana-dashboards.energy.yaml. Panel titles are German, matching the existing dashboard; comments and code stay English.

Panel Kind Content Erzeugung gegen Erwartung timeseries (new) home:power_generation:watts against solar:expected_power:watts — the core deliverable Anlagenleistung stat (new) solar:performance_ratio * 100, in % Anlagengesundheit (existing row) timeseries gains max by (string) (solar_irradiance_tilted_wm2), so a diverging string reads against its own reference Datenquellen (existing) gains up{job="openmeteo-exporter"}

The ConfigMap holding the dashboard must go through configMapGenerator so the content hash rolls the Grafana sidecar, per the existing pattern.

docs.title: Credential Hygiene
docs.text:
docs/energy-metrics-api.md contains a live Grafana service-account token, says in its own header that it must not be committed, and is not gitignored. The repository is public and no pre-commit hook recognises a Grafana token, so a single git add docs/ would leak it.

  • Add docs/energy-metrics-api.md to .gitignore.
  • Document the array parameters from this design in that file's "The physical setup" section, which currently says only "two panels".
  • The file itself is never committed. Only the .gitignore line is.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
apps/solar/openmeteo-exporter.py            new   ~50 lines, stdlib only
apps/solar/k8s.openmeteo-exporter.yaml      new   Deployment + Service + ServiceMonitor
apps/solar/k8s.np.openmeteo-exporter.yaml   new   CiliumNetworkPolicy
apps/solar/kustomization.yaml               edit  + configMapGenerator, + resources
apps/solar/secrets.enc.yaml                 edit  + latitude, longitude (SOPS)
apps/monitoring/k8s.prometheusrule.energy.yaml    edit  3 rules, 3 alerts
apps/monitoring/ks8.grafana-dashboards.energy.yaml edit 2 new panels, 2 amended
.gitignore                                  edit  + docs/energy-metrics-api.md
docs/energy-metrics-api.md                  edit  array parameters — NEVER COMMITTED

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
1. Run openmeteo-exporter.py locally against the live API; confirm the two GTI values differ as expected for NE vs SW at the current hour. 1b. grep -rn the working tree for the coordinate digits before committing, and confirm /metrics output and pod logs contain neither.
  2. kustomize build apps/solar --enable-helm --enable-alpha-plugins --enable-exec
  3. scripts/kubeconform-validate.sh apps/solar apps/monitoring
  4. pre-commit run --all-files
  5. After sync: up{job="openmeteo-exporter"} == 1.
  6. Confirm egress actually works — hubble observe --namespace solar — before assuming toFQDNs took effect.
  7. On the next clear day, check solar:performance_ratio lands near 0.68 and adjust the literal if not.

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Forecast and load-shifting panels (follow-up issue)
  • Historical irradiance backfill for past days
  • Any new Grafana plugin or datasource
  • Modelling temperature coefficients, shading, or angle-of-incidence losses; all of that is absorbed into the single performance-ratio constant

docs.title: Addendum, 2026-09-07 evening: per-string, after first contact with reality
docs.text:
The design above compares aggregate generation against an aggregate expectation. Deployment showed that cannot work here, and the deployed system differs accordingly.

What the first measurements showed. At 18:10 local, pv1 was at 0.67 of its modelled irradiance while pv2 was at 0.19, with both producing roughly the same absolute power. The operator confirmed the cause: pv2 faces south-west and is shaded by a tree from the early afternoon. The operator also confirmed the string mapping — pv1 is the north-east panel, pv2 the south-west one — which until then had only been inferred from the order of a sentence.

Why the aggregate design was wrong. The shading is permanent and predictable, so an aggregate expected curve overstates afternoon output every single day. A reference that is reliably wrong at the same time daily teaches the reader to ignore the panel — the exact failure the "ideal ceiling only" option was rejected for. The aggregate ratio was already 0.291, below the 0.40 threshold, with only the ideal_power > 300 guard keeping the alert quiet.

What changed.

  • Three per-string recording rules: solar:ideal_power_by_string:watts, solar:expected_power_by_string:watts, solar:performance_ratio_by_string.
  • SolarArrayUnderperforming replaced by SolarStringUnderperforming: per string, and only between 07:00 and 12:00 UTC, before the shading begins. hour() is UTC, so the window drifts an hour across DST — harmless when the shading starts in the afternoon, and PromQL cannot express local time.
  • Panel 18 plots each string against its own model; panel 19 shows the ratio per string.
  • The aggregate rules are kept: they carry history and still answer "how is the whole array doing right now".

One basis difference to keep in mind. Per-string actuals are DC, because there is no per-string AC value; the aggregate uses AC. A DC ratio excludes inverter conversion loss and the inverter's own draw, so it reads slightly higher for identical conditions. The 0.68 constant is reused for now and needs its own calibration.

Verified after deployment. For pv1, expected 40.6 W against an actual 40.1 W — the reference sits on the measurement, which validates the API, the geometry, the peak-power figures and the constant for an unshaded string.

Two deployment defects, both fixed. DNS failed because ndots:5 makes the resolver try three search-domain permutations first, which a narrow matchName rule caused Cilium to answer REFUSED, and musl treats REFUSED as fatal (commit 102c830b). Scrapes then timed out because Prometheus's own egress allowlist did not include the new exporter — a namespaced CiliumNetworkPolicy's toEndpoints: - {} only matches its own namespace (commit f702f104). The second one is deceptive: the target's ingress rule is correct and its BPF byte counters sitting at zero are what proves the packets never arrived.

docs.title: td-sync Server im k3s-Cluster — Design
docs.text:
• Datum: 2026-09-07
  • td-Issue: td-02c66e
  • Upstream: https://github.com/marcus/td (v0.65.0)
  • Ops-Guide: docs/sync-server-ops-guide.md im Upstream-Repo

docs.title: Ziel
docs.text: Den td-Sync-Server im bestehenden k3s-Cluster betreiben, damit der lokale td-CLI seine Issues über mehrere Geräte und AI-Sessions hinweg synchronisieren kann. Erreichbarkeit ausschließlich intern (LAN/VPN). Versions-Updates laufen automatisiert über Renovate.

docs.title: Recherche-Befunde, die das Design bestimmen
docs.text:
Drei Eigenschaften von td-sync weichen von dem ab, was der Ops-Guide auf den ersten Blick nahelegt:

  1. Kein publiziertes Container-Image. marcus/td released ausschließlich Binaries (v0.65.0: linux/darwin, amd64/arm64). Weder GHCR noch Docker Hub führen ein Image. Der Guide baut selbst aus deploy/Dockerfile.

  2. Litestream deckt nur server.db ab. deploy/litestream.yml listet genau eine DB. Die eigentlichen Issue-Daten liegen in Per-Projekt-Datenbanken unter SYNC_PROJECT_DATA_DIR (/data/projects), die dynamisch angelegt werden. Litestream 0.3.x kennt keine Globs, kann sie also nicht erfassen. Das mitgelieferte Backup schützt die Metadaten, nicht den Inhalt.

  3. Login erfordert zwingend E-Mail. internal/email/ implementiert nur cloudflare.go, log.go und memory.go — kein SMTP. Das im Cluster vorhandene Postfix-Relay ist ohne Upstream-Änderung nicht nutzbar. Der Bestätigungslink wird nicht im Terminal angezeigt; der Login schließt erst ab, wenn der Link aufgerufen wurde.

Weiter relevant:

  • /metricz liefert JSON (internal/api/metrics.go, MetricsSnapshot), kein Prometheus-Exposition-Format.
  • /healthz gibt 500 zurück, wenn die DB nicht erreichbar ist.
  • Der Entrypoint startet Litestream unbedingt und wrappt td-sync darin (litestream replicate -exec "td-sync"). Ein Deployment ohne Litestream erforderte ein Command-Override.
  • td taggt sauber semver (v0.65.0, v0.64.0, …) — für Renovate unproblematisch.
  • Die Forge-Registry gibt auf /v2/ zwar 401, beantwortet aber den Standard-Bearer-Challenge anonym. Gegen madic/docker-samba getestet: die Tag-Liste kommt ohne Credentials zurück. Renovates Docker-Datasource macht genau diesen Flow, kann die Registry also lesen.

docs.title: Getroffene Entscheidungen
docs.text: Entscheidung Gewählt Alternative(n) Begründung Erreichbarkeit Nur intern Cloudflare Tunnel, öffentliches Traefik Sync wird nur zuhause bzw. über VPN gebraucht; kleinste Angriffsfläche Image-Build Forgejo Actions in madic/docker-td → forge.geekbundle.org GitHub-Fork + Actions → ghcr.io; lokal bauen; initContainer lädt Release-Binary Deckt sich mit madic/docker-samba, docker-radarr, docker-nzbget; Repo existiert bereits Backup Longhorn-PVC + restic-CronJob Nur Longhorn; zusätzlich Litestream→versitygw (S3) Nur restic erfasst die Projekt-DBs; Off-Site-Mirror nach Wasabi läuft bereits Auth-Mail SYNC_EMAIL_PROVIDER=log Cloudflare Email API; SMTP-Provider upstream beitragen Login passiert selten (Credentials landen in ~/.config/td/auth.json); null Zusatzinfrastruktur Update-Automatisierung Renovate im Build-Repo (Forgejo Actions) + bestehendes Renovate in k3s-git-ops Cron-Poll im Build-Workflow; manuell Trackt neben TD_VERSION auch die Base-Images; Review-Gate an beiden Stellen

docs.title: Architektur
docs.text:
Zwei getrennte Repositories:

forge.geekbundle.org/madic/docker-td              (Build, außerhalb k3s-git-ops)
  ├─ Dockerfile                    ARG TD_VERSION  ← Renovate bumpt das
  ├─ renovate.json5                platform=forgejo
  └─ .forgejo/workflows/
       ├─ build.yaml               push auf main → Image bauen und pushen
       └─ renovate.yaml            Cron → Renovate
                    │
                    │ forge.geekbundle.org/madic/td-sync:vX.Y.Z@sha256:…
                    ▼
k3s-git-ops/apps/td-sync/                          (Deployment)
  └─ von ArgoCD via apps/argo-cd-apps/62-td-sync.yaml ausgerollt

Lokaler Klon des Build-Repos: /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/docker-td (Remote ssh://git@forge.geekbundle.org/madic/docker-td.git, bisher nur ein README). Vorlage für Aufbau und Renovate-Config ist /home/mne-adm/Git/personal/github.com/container-restic.

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
Anders als im Ops-Guide klont das Dockerfile den Upstream selbst. Damit ist TD_VERSION eine einzelne, von Renovate pflegbare Zeile, und entrypoint.sh sowie litestream.yml kommen unverändert aus dem Checkout — es gibt keine Kopien davon zu pflegen.

# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=marcus/td
ARG TD_VERSION="v0.65.0"

FROM golang:1.27-alpine AS builder
ARG TD_VERSION
RUN apk add --no-cache git
WORKDIR /src
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "${TD_VERSION}" https://github.com/marcus/td.git .
RUN go mod download
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/td-sync ./cmd/td-sync

FROM litestream/litestream:0.3.13 AS litestream

FROM alpine:3.21
RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates tzdata wget sqlite
COPY --from=litestream /usr/local/bin/litestream /usr/local/bin/litestream
COPY --from=builder /out/td-sync /usr/local/bin/td-sync
COPY --from=builder /src/deploy/litestream.yml /etc/litestream.yml
COPY --from=builder /src/deploy/entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod +x /entrypoint.sh
VOLUME /data
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]

Unterschiede zum Upstream-deploy/Dockerfile:

  • Der Upstream baut aus dem Build-Context; wir klonen im Builder-Stage.
  • sqlite kommt zusätzlich ins Runtime-Image (Begründung im Backup-Abschnitt).

ARG TD_VERSION vor dem ersten FROM ist ein globales ARG und muss im Builder-Stage ohne Wert erneut deklariert werden, damit es dort sichtbar ist.

Beim ersten Build zu prüfen: golang:1.27-alpine und litestream/litestream:0.3.13 müssen als Tags existieren. Danach hält Renovates nativer Dockerfile-Manager sie aktuell.

docs.title: Build-Workflow
docs.text:
.forgejo/workflows/build.yaml, runs-on: ubuntu-latest (der Runner läuft außerhalb des Clusters). Trigger: Push auf main mit Pfadfilter auf Dockerfile und die Workflow-Datei, plus workflow_dispatch.

Bewusst keine docker/*-Actions, sondern nackte docker-CLI-Steps: uses:-Referenzen lösen auf Forgejo gegen DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL auf, und ob die docker/*-Actions dort liegen, ist instanzabhängig. Nur actions/checkout wird verwendet — das ist sowohl auf code.forgejo.org als auch auf GitHub vorhanden.

Ablauf:

  1. Checkout
  2. TD_VERSION aus dem Dockerfile lesen (sed), als Step-Output setzen
  3. docker login forge.geekbundle.org mit ${{ github.actor }} und dem automatisch bereitgestellten Actions-Token
  4. docker build, taggen mit :${TD_VERSION} und :latest, beides pushen

Der Registry-Login über den automatischen Actions-Token ist beim ersten Lauf zu verifizieren; setzt voraus, dass Package-Write für Actions aktiv ist.

docs.title: Renovate im Build-Repo
docs.text:
.forgejo/workflows/renovate.yaml (Cron, täglich) fährt Renovate mit platform: forgejo und endpoint: https://forge.geekbundle.org/api/v1 gegen madic/docker-td.

renovate.json5 übernimmt die Konventionen aus container-restic (onboarding: false, automergeType: 'branch', ignoreTests: true, major.automerge: false, minimumReleaseAge: '5 days', minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: 'timestamp-optional', internalChecksFilter: 'strict') und erweitert extends um den Preset customManagers:dockerfileVersions. Dessen Regex matcht genau das oben gewählte Muster (# renovate: … gefolgt von ARG …_VERSION="…") — ein eigener Custom-Manager ist nicht nötig.

platformAutomerge bleibt aus: Forgejo unterstützt es erst ab v10, und mit automergeType: 'branch' merged Renovate ohnehin selbst.

Zwei Secrets:

Secret Zweck RENOVATE_TOKEN Forgejo-PAT. Scopes: repo (RW), user (R), issue (RW), organization (R), read:packages GITHUB_COM_TOKEN GitHub-PAT (nur öffentliche Repos, read-only). Die github-releases-Datasource fragt github.com ab und läuft ohne Token schnell ins Rate-Limit

Optional, falls Docker Hub für golang/alpine/litestream limitiert: hostRules mit Docker-Hub-Credentials.

docs.title: Die Update-Kette
docs.text:
Renovate (Forgejo)  bumpt ARG TD_VERSION   → Branch-Automerge auf main
        ↓
build.yaml          baut, pusht td-sync:vX.Y.Z + :latest
        ↓
Renovate (GitHub)   sieht den neuen Tag in der Forge-Registry
        ↓
PR in k3s-git-ops   aktualisiert Tag + Digest in k8s.td-sync.yaml

Damit das letzte Glied greift, muss das Image in k8s.td-sync.yaml als :vX.Y.Z@sha256:… referenziert werden, nicht digest-only. Die bestehenden Forge-Images (docker-samba@sha256:… usw.) sind digest-only gepinnt; Renovate hat dort kein currentValue und trackt sie deshalb heute nicht. Mit Tag greift der bereits konfigurierte kubernetes-Manager (Pattern /apps/.+/k8s\..*\.yaml$/, passt auf apps/td-sync/k8s.td-sync.yaml) und aktualisiert Tag und Digest gemeinsam.

Major-Updates werden in beiden Repos nicht automerged. Weil td auf 0.x steht und ein Minor-Sprung dort brechen darf, bekommt marcus/td zusätzlich eine explizite packageRule mit matchUpdateTypes: ['minor'], automerge: false — v0.65 → v0.66 landet damit als PR zum Anschauen statt automatisch zu mergen. (Sich darauf zu verlassen, dass Renovate 0.x-Minor von sich aus wie Major behandelt, wäre eine ungeprüfte Annahme.)

docs.title: Cluster-App
docs.text:
apps/td-sync/:

Datei Inhalt k8s.td-sync.yaml Namespace, ServiceAccount, Deployment, Service k8s.pvc.yaml longhorn-pvc-td-sync, 2Gi, RWO ingress.enc.yaml SOPS-verschlüsselt, Host td.internal.neese-web.de k8s.np.td-sync-default-deny.yaml CiliumNetworkPolicy, Default-Deny k8s.np.td-sync.yaml CiliumNetworkPolicy für td-sync k8s.backup-cronjob.yaml restic-CronJob + zugehörige CiliumNetworkPolicy backup-env-configuration-td-sync.enc.yaml restic-Konfiguration, SOPS kustomization.yaml Ressourcen + ksops-Generator, sync-wave: "62" kustomize-secret-generator.yaml ksops für ingress.enc.yaml und backup-env-configuration-td-sync.enc.yaml

Dazu apps/argo-cd-apps/62-td-sync.yaml (Sync-Wave 62, zwischen 60-semaphore und 64-downloader-lidarr) und der Eintrag in apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml.

Namespace: td-sync, mit Label goldilocks.fairwinds.com/enabled: "true".

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
• replicas: 1, strategy: Recreate. SQLite verträgt keine zwei gleichzeitigen Writer, und die Longhorn-PVC ist ReadWriteOnce. Ein RollingUpdate würde kurzzeitig zwei Pods erzeugen und scheitern bzw. Daten gefährden.
  • Image: forge.geekbundle.org/madic/td-sync:v0.65.0@sha256:…
  • Port 8080 (http)
  • Readiness- und Liveness-Probe: httpGet auf /healthz
  • resources.requests: 50m CPU / 64Mi RAM. Goldilocks/VPA korrigiert später auf Basis echter Werte.
  • securityContext: runAsUser: 1000, runAsGroup: 1000, fsGroup: 1000, runAsNonRoot: true; Container: allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities.drop: [ALL]. Das Upstream-Image setzt kein USER, würde also als root laufen; fsGroup sorgt dafür, dass das Volume für UID 1000 schreibbar ist.

Kein imagePullSecret: die Forge-Registry erlaubt anonymen Pull, die bestehenden madic/docker-*-Deployments arbeiten ebenfalls ohne.

Volumes: eine PVC, zwei Mounts über subPath:

Mount subPath Zweck /data data server.db und projects/*.db /backups backups Litestream-File-Replica von server.db

Der Entrypoint startet Litestream unbedingt. Statt das zu umgehen, bekommt /backups einen echten Mount: die File-Replica überlebt Neustarts und wird vom restic-Job mitgesichert. Sie ist ein konsistenter Zusatz-Snapshot von server.db, ersetzt aber das restic-Backup nicht (Projekt-DBs fehlen).

Environment:

SYNC_LISTEN_ADDR       = :8080
SYNC_BASE_URL          = https://td.internal.neese-web.de
SYNC_SERVER_DB_PATH    = /data/server.db
SYNC_PROJECT_DATA_DIR  = /data/projects
SYNC_ALLOW_SIGNUP      = true   → nach Erstaccount auf false
SYNC_EMAIL_PROVIDER    = log
SYNC_LOG_FORMAT        = json
SYNC_LOG_LEVEL         = info
SYNC_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT  = 60s

Keine Werte davon sind geheim; sie stehen im Klartext im Deployment. Nur Ingress (Domain) und restic-Config werden verschlüsselt.

docs.title: Ingress
docs.text:
Host td.internal.neese-web.de, nach dem Muster der internen Apps:

  • traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.entrypoints: web239,websecure239
  • router.tls: "true"
  • router.middlewares: traefik-redirect@kubernetescrd
  • tls.secretName: wildcard-cloudflare-production-02

Kein Authelia-ForwardAuth. Die anderen internen Apps setzen authelia-forwardauth-authelia@kubernetescrd, hier würde es die API brechen: der td-CLI authentifiziert sich mit Bearer-Token gegen /v1/... und kann keinen SSO-Redirect verarbeiten. td bringt eigene Authentifizierung (Device-Flow + API-Keys) mit.

docs.title: NetworkPolicies
docs.text:
Default-Deny für den Namespace, dazu eine App-Policy:

  • Ingress: nur von Traefik (k8s:app.kubernetes.io/instance: traefik-kube-system, Namespace kube-system) auf Port 8080
  • Egress: nur CoreDNS (53/UDP + 53/TCP)

Mehr braucht td-sync nicht: der log-Provider verschickt keine Mails, Litestream repliziert nur auf das lokale Dateisystem, und es gibt keine Outbound-Calls.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
restic-CronJob nach dem etablierten Muster des Repos (siehe docs/backup.md): Ziel ist der rest-server im Namespace backup, der tägliche rclone-Mirror nach Wasabi und die zentrale Retention-Policy greifen automatisch.

  • podAffinity auf den td-sync-Pod — die Longhorn-PVC ist RWO, beide Pods müssen auf demselben Node laufen
  • Das Skript kommt über den Reflector in den Namespace: die ConfigMap crontab-backup-script in longhorn hat reflection-auto-enabled: "true" ohne Namespace-Einschränkung, wird also überall gespiegelt. Keine Änderung an apps/backup-script/ nötig.
  • restic-Container: ghcr.io/madic-creates/container-restic (Digest wie in den anderen Jobs), envFrom auf backup-env-configuration-td-sync
  • Eigene CiliumNetworkPolicy: DNS, Pushgateway 9091, rest-server 8000, world:443 für ntfy im Fehlerfall

docs.title: Konsistenz der SQLite-Snapshots
docs.text:
Ein direkter restic backup auf /data liest foo.db, foo.db-wal und foo.db-shm nacheinander, nicht atomar. Läuft parallel ein Write, kann der Snapshot zerrissen und beim Restore unbrauchbar sein.

Lösung analog zum bestehenden MariaDB-Job (initContainer erzeugt den Dump, restic versendet ihn):

  1. initContainer mit unserem eigenen td-sync-Image führt für server.db und jede projects/*.db ein sqlite3 <db> ".backup /snapshot/<name>.db" aus, Ziel ist ein emptyDir.
  2. restic-Container sichert ausschließlich dieses emptyDir.

Deshalb sqlite im Dockerfile: kein apk add zur Laufzeit (das bräuchte Egress zum Alpine-CDN und eine entsprechend weite NetworkPolicy), kein Fremd-Image, und das Image ist ohnehin unter unserer Kontrolle.

Die PVC wird im Backup-Pod read-write gemountet. SQLite braucht beim Öffnen einer WAL-Datenbank Schreibzugriff auf die -shm-Datei; das readOnly: true des Grafana-Jobs funktioniert hier nicht.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
/metricz liefert JSON und ist nicht direkt scrapebar. Für den ersten Ausbau:

  • Blackbox-Exporter-Probe auf https://td.internal.neese-web.de/healthz — der Exporter läuft bereits (apps/monitoring-blackbox-exporter/)
  • die bestehenden generischen Pod-/Deployment-Alerts

Ein json_exporter für /metricz wäre nachrüstbar, ist für einen Single-User-Sync-Server aber unverhältnismäßig.

docs.title: Rollout
docs.text:
1. Build-Repo docker-td befüllen (Dockerfile, Workflows, renovate.json5), Secrets setzen, Build auslösen, Digest notieren
  2. apps/td-sync/ und den ArgoCD-Application-Eintrag committen und pushen, zunächst mit SYNC_ALLOW_SIGNUP=true
  3. ArgoCD-Sync abwarten, /healthz prüfen
  4. td config set sync.url https://td.internal.neese-web.de
  5. td auth login, Bestätigungslink aus kubectl logs -n td-sync deploy/td-sync holen und im Browser aufrufen
  6. SYNC_ALLOW_SIGNUP=false committen und syncen lassen
  7. Migration verifizieren (siehe unten), dann pro Projekt td sync-project create "<name>" und td sync
  8. Renovate-Kette einmal manuell durchspielen (workflow_dispatch auf renovate.yaml), um zu sehen, dass TD_VERSION erkannt wird

docs.title: Migration des bestehenden Bestands
docs.text:
Vor Schritt 7 zu klären: ob td sync-project create + td sync den vorhandenen lokalen .todos/-Bestand vollständig hochlädt oder erst ab dem Zeitpunkt der Verknüpfung neue Events repliziert. Der Sync-Setup-Guide sagt dazu nichts.

Vorgehen: zuerst gegen ein Wegwerf-Projekt mit ein paar Test-Issues prüfen, ob die Historie ankommt. Erst danach die echten Projekte anbinden. .todos/ wird vorher gesichert.

docs.title: Bewusst nicht im Scope
docs.text:
• Multi-User-Betrieb, Einladungen, Rollen (td sync-project invite)
  • Öffentliche Erreichbarkeit über Cloudflare Tunnel
  • Litestream-Replikation nach versitygw/S3
  • json_exporter für /metricz
  • Ein SMTP-Provider als Upstream-Beitrag
  • Der in-cluster forgejo-runner. apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml:59 hat 65-forgejo-runner.yaml auskommentiert (Commit 4a4bdc28, 2025-12-15, „Disable forgejo runner for now"), Namespace und ArgoCD-Application existieren nicht. Gebaut wird auf einem Runner außerhalb des Clusters. Ob die Karteileiche im Repo bleibt oder aufgeräumt wird, ist eine eigene Entscheidung.

docs.title: Design: Testing the Navidrome Podcast-UX Fork as a Parallel Instance
docs.text: Date: 2026-09-08 Issue: td-e7c3cf

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Evaluate search5/navidrome@feat-podcast-ux-improvements/5420 (upstream PR navidrome/navidrome#5949, which addresses issue #5420; HEAD 07cf48cb8c927b5aa062309c352536ef8752a6d4) in the real cluster, against real library data, without putting the production Navidrome instance at risk.

The fork publishes no container image, so one has to be built. It is rebased on Navidrome master — go 1.27, mpv-based playback, multi-library support — which is far ahead of the deployed ghcr.io/navidrome/navidrome:0.63.2.

docs.title: The Constraint That Shapes Everything
docs.text:
Navidrome runs goose migrations against navidrome.db at startup. The branch carries five podcast migrations:

db/migrations/20260427165650_add_podcast.go
db/migrations/20260427184047_add_podcast_downloaded_bytes.go
db/migrations/20260428000000_add_podcast20.go
db/migrations/20260428120000_add_podcast_tier3.go
db/migrations/20260428200000_add_podcast_metadata.go

Pointing this build at the production data folder would migrate the database to a master-era schema. 0.63.2 cannot read that schema, so there would be no way back short of restoring a backup. Everything below follows from refusing to accept that risk.

A second consequence, from core/podcasts/podcasts.go:301 and :349: episodes are downloaded into ${DataFolder}/podcasts/<channelID>/, and the code registers a virtual library whose root is DataFolder. Running the fork therefore writes both files and an extra library row. There is no feature flag gating this — conf/configuration.go has no podcast setting at all.

docs.title: Scope Decision
docs.text:
In scope: a second, fully isolated Navidrome deployment in namespace media, running the fork against a point-in-time copy of the production database, reachable at music-test.k8s.neese-web.de.

Out of scope: merging test-instance state back into production. Once the copy is taken the two instances diverge permanently. Playlists, play counts, and podcast subscriptions created in the test instance are throwaway.

Out of scope: building the image in Forgejo CI. That is the established pattern for the long-lived custom images (td-sync, docker-samba, docker-nzbget, docker-radarr), but this is a one-off evaluation and a local build gets there faster with a warm cache. If the fork turns into something permanent, moving the build to madic/docker-navidrome is the follow-up.

docs.title: 1. Image Build
docs.text:
The fork's Dockerfile is a standard buildx multi-stage build. --target final pulls the binary from the build-alpine stage; the osxcross stage feeds only the standalone-distribution build stage and is never touched by a native amd64 build of final. BuildKit is mandatory — the Dockerfile uses heredoc RUN <<EOT blocks and --mount=type=cache.

git clone --depth 1 --branch feat-podcast-ux-improvements/5420 \
  https://github.com/search5/navidrome.git /tmp/navidrome-5420
cd /tmp/navidrome-5420

docker login forge.geekbundle.org
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  --target final \
  --build-arg GIT_SHA=07cf48cb \
  --build-arg GIT_TAG=5420-podcast-ux \
  -t forge.geekbundle.org/madic/navidrome-test:5420-07cf48cb \
  --push .

GIT_SHA and GIT_TAG are load-bearing, not cosmetic: they are linked into consts.gitSha / consts.gitTag via ldflags and are the only way to confirm in the running UI which build is live.

The registry package stays public. No manifest in this repo uses imagePullSecrets for forge.geekbundle.org, and this instance must not become the exception.

After the push, resolve the digest and pin it in the deployment, matching the convention used by every other forge.geekbundle.org image in the repo:

docker buildx imagetools inspect \
  forge.geekbundle.org/madic/navidrome-test:5420-07cf48cb --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}'

docs.title: 2. Cluster Manifests
docs.text:
The test resources live inside apps/navidrome/, not in a separate app directory. The existing ArgoCD Application 33-navidrome (sync wave 33, source path apps/navidrome) then manages them with no new Application manifest and no new entry in apps/argo-cd-apps/kustomization.yaml. Because that Application has prune: true, teardown is exactly "delete the files and push".

New files:

File Purpose k8s.test.deployment.yaml Deployment navidrome-test k8s.test.service.yaml Service navidrome-test k8s.np.navidrome-test.yaml CiliumNetworkPolicy for the test pod ingress-test.enc.yaml SOPS-encrypted IngressRoutes

Modified: kustomization.yaml (three resources added) and kustomize-secret-generator.yaml (one ksops file added).

docs.title: The label must differ
docs.text:
The production Service selects app.kubernetes.io/name: navidrome. If the test pod carried that same label, Traefik would load-balance production traffic onto an unvetted fork build — silently, with no error anywhere. The test Deployment therefore uses app.kubernetes.io/name: navidrome-test throughout: pod template labels, Deployment selector, and Service selector.

That label change also means the existing CiliumNetworkPolicy navidrome does not cover the test pod — its endpointSelector matches the production label. A second policy is required, otherwise the default-deny posture leaves the test pod unreachable and unable to resolve DNS.

docs.title: Deployment differences from production
docs.text:
Everything else is copied from k8s.deployment.yaml unchanged — same securityContext (runAsUser: 1001, runAsGroup: 1002, fsGroup: 1002), same nodeSelector (node-role/workload: zfs), same dnsConfig (ndots: 1), same strategy: Recreate.

Setting Production Test Why image ghcr.io/navidrome/navidrome:0.63.2 forge.geekbundle.org/madic/navidrome-test@sha256:… the fork build config-vol hostPath /vol_raidz1/container-scheduler/navidrome …/navidrome-test schema isolation music-vol mount read-write readOnly: true the fork must not be able to touch the library ND_SCANSCHEDULE @every 1h "0" the copied DB already holds the scanned library

ND_MUSICFOLDER, ND_LOGLEVEL, ND_REVERSEPROXYWHITELIST, ND_ENABLEUSEREDITING, ND_ENABLESHARING and TZ are carried over as-is.

docs.title: Secrets are reused, deliberately
docs.text: The test Deployment references the existing navidrome-secrets Secret. This is a correctness requirement, not convenience: ND_PASSWORDENCRYPTIONKEY must match the key that encrypted the passwords in the copied database, or no user can log in. Reusing the Secret makes that impossible to get wrong. No new *.enc.yaml secret file is created.

docs.title: Ingress
docs.text:
ingress-test.enc.yaml mirrors the three production IngressRoutes on host music-test.k8s.neese-web.de, entrypoint websecure:

Path rule Middlewares PathPrefix('/') traefik/redirect, authelia/forwardauth-authelia PathPrefix('/rest/') && !Query('c','NavidromeUI') traefik/redirect, authelia/forwardauth-authelia-basic-forward-auth PathPrefix('/share/') traefik/redirect

All three point at Service navidrome-test port 4533, and carry over tls: {} and observability.accessLogs: true from the production routes.

The host falls under wildcard-cloudflare-production-01, which Traefik already serves on the web/websecure entrypoints — no Certificate resource and no cert-manager change is needed.

The file is encrypted because .sops.yaml's encrypted_regex covers hostnames, matching how ingress.enc.yaml is handled today. Like that file, it is emitted through ksops rather than listed under resources:.

docs.title: Network policy
docs.text:
k8s.np.navidrome-test.yaml is k8s.np.navidrome.yaml with the endpointSelector changed to app.kubernetes.io/name: navidrome-test. The rules themselves need no change:

  • Ingress from Traefik (kube-system) and Authelia (authelia) on 4533
  • Egress to CoreDNS on 53/UDP+TCP
  • Egress to world on 80 and 443 — which already covers podcast RSS feeds and episode downloads, so podcast fetching works without a policy change

docs.title: 3. Data Copy
docs.text:
Copying a live SQLite database with cp yields a torn snapshot: the -wal and -shm sidecars are not captured atomically alongside the main file. SQLite's .backup command is online-safe and produces a consistent single file.

On the ZFS node:

D=/vol_raidz1/container-scheduler
mkdir -p "$D/navidrome-test"
sqlite3 "$D/navidrome/navidrome.db" ".backup '$D/navidrome-test/navidrome.db'"
chown -R 1001:1002 "$D/navidrome-test"

Only navidrome.db is copied. Cache directories are left behind; the instance rebuilds them.

If shell access to the node is undesirable, the same three commands run as a one-off Job with both host paths mounted — permitted by the GitOps rules as a cluster-state operation not represented in Git. The Navidrome image is alpine:3.22-based and ships sqlite, so it needs no other image.

From this point the two databases diverge permanently. See Scope Decision.

docs.title: 4. Verification
docs.text:
In order — each step gates the next:

  1. kubectl logs -n media deploy/navidrome-test — the five podcast migrations apply cleanly and the server reports it is listening on 4533
  2. Log in at music-test.k8s.neese-web.de with production credentials. Success proves the encryption key and the database copy are consistent with each other.
  3. kubectl get endpoints -n media navidrome returns only the production pod IP. This is the check that the label separation held.
  4. Subscribe to a podcast feed and download an episode; confirm files land under /vol_raidz1/container-scheduler/navidrome-test/podcasts/
  5. Exercise the actual subject of the evaluation — the PR's podcast UX changes

docs.title: 5. Teardown
docs.text:
Delete the four new files, revert the two modified files, push. ArgoCD prunes the Deployment, Service, CiliumNetworkPolicy and IngressRoutes.

/vol_raidz1/container-scheduler/navidrome-test/ is not managed by ArgoCD and must be removed by hand. Depending on how many episodes were downloaded it may hold a non-trivial amount of data.

The production instance is never modified at any point, so there is nothing to roll back on that side.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Test pod absorbs production traffic distinct app.kubernetes.io/name label; verified explicitly in step 3 Fork writes to the music library readOnly: true on the music mount Users cannot log in to the test instance production navidrome-secrets reused, so ND_PASSWORDENCRYPTIONKEY matches Unvetted build exposed externally Authelia forward-auth on / and /rest/, same as production Torn database copy sqlite3 .backup instead of cp Podcast downloads fill the pool ZFS pool, monitored; removed at teardown

docs.title: Addendum 2026-09-08: The Branch Does Not Compile
docs.text:
The first build attempt failed. Root cause, reproduced both in Docker and with a native go build:

core/podcasts/podcasts.go:8:2:   "net" imported and not used
core/podcasts/podcasts.go:10:2:  "net/url" imported and not used
core/podcasts/podcasts.go:315:12: undefined: validateURL
core/podcasts/podcasts.go:539:12: undefined: validateURL

validateURL is called twice but never defined. The only definition in the tree is conf/configuration.go:906, a different two-argument function in another package. The base branch feat/podcast contains no reference to validateURL at all, so this is an incomplete commit by the PR author, not a bad rebase.

The function was never deleted — it was never written. Four commits within 65 seconds on 2026-09-07, all web-editor edits, add everything around it: cb193a0e8a the two imports, 037fcfd8d7 the call in fetchAndParse, a2aaf3e9d6 /podcast/preview behind adminOnlyMiddleware, 07cf48cb8c the call in doDownload. That burst is a security hardening pass, so an SSRF guard was the intent — which is what the net import is for.

No reusable helper exists in the tree: conf.validateURL is unexported with a different signature, the plugin host client's check is a method coupled to per-plugin permissions, and core/artwork/agent_images.go:35 rolls its own inline. A local function matches the codebase convention.

apps/navidrome/navidrome-pr5949.patch supplies it, mirroring the scheme and host checks of conf.validateURL and the address check of isPrivateOrLoopback in plugins/host_httpclient.go. Like that one it inspects IP literals only and does not stop DNS rebinding.

This leaves the branch's own suite at 78 passed / 23 failed; every failure is the guard rejecting httptest fixtures on 127.0.0.1. A scheme-only variant passes 101/101 but provides no SSRF protection. The guard was kept because the test pod's CiliumNetworkPolicy permits egress to world, which in Cilium includes the home LAN — so an attacker-supplied feed URL would otherwise reach it. Neither the Docker build nor pre-commit runs those tests.

Consequence for the evaluation: what runs in the cluster is PR + patch, not the PR verbatim.

The build step therefore gains a git apply between clone and build.

docs.title: Second defect: existing databases cannot be migrated
docs.text:
The first deploy of the patched image still failed, this time at startup:

Failed to apply new migrations
error: found 5 missing migrations before current version 20260703013908

The five podcast migrations carry April 2026 timestamps while the branch is rebased on master, whose schema is already past them. db/db.go:107 calls goose.UpContext(ctx, db, migrationsFolder) with no options, and goose refuses out-of-order migrations by default.

Reproduced as a controlled experiment rather than assumed: a database driven to the current schema, then stripped of the five podcast versions and their tables, reproduces the fatal error exactly with an unpatched binary. With goose.WithAllowMissing() all five apply, the eight podcast_* tables appear, the versions are recorded, and the pre-existing tables are untouched.

The patch adds that option. It is safe here only because the five migrations are self-contained — they create and alter podcast_* tables they own and touch nothing else. Upstream should renumber them instead; the flag relaxes ordering for every migration, not just these.

This is the more serious of the two defects for the PR: the compile error blocks anyone building it, but the migration ordering blocks every existing installation from upgrading.
